The clause «توتون ...» «[Translator's note: so in the source, for «تؤتون».]» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تأتنّني به ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.
The clause «آتوه ...» «[Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «آتوه», whereas the i'rab above cites «أتوه».]» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «الله ... وكيل» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «نقول ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(موثقا), a mīmī maṣdar from the verb وثق يثق; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, because it is a mithāl (first-radical weak) verb whose fāʾ is deleted in the imperfect.
(يحاط), in it there is an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion for the passive: the active imperfect is يحيط; when the letter before the last was given fatḥa and the fatḥa was transferred to the letter before the yāʾ because of its quiescence, the yāʾ, originally voweled, was converted to an alif because the letter before it had fatḥa. And the yāʾ in (يحيط) is converted from a wāw — its simple-form imperfect is يحوط — and the origin is يحوط with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the wāw; when the kasra was felt heavy on the wāw it was made quiescent and the vowel transferred to the letter before it; the letter before the quiescent wāw was given kasra, so it was converted to yāʾ and became يحيط.

safi-cedvel:23-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (راودت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and (الهاء) an object pronoun; (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (في بيتها) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (عن نفسه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (راودت), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (غلّقت) like راودت, the fāʿil being "she"; (الأبواب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunctive; (قالت) like راودت, the fāʿil being "she"; (هيت) a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the past, meaning "I have made myself ready" [Note: or a verbal noun of the imperative, meaning "come forward" or "hurry", the fāʿil being "you".], (اللام) a preposition — and it is the lām of clarification (tabyīn) [Note: «i.e. clarifying the object, that is, the one addressed ... as though she were saying: "I say to you" or "the address is to you", as in سقيا لك and رعيا لك» — end of quotation, summarized from al-Jamal.] — and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقول ("I say"); (قال) a past verb, the fāʿil being "he"; (معاذ) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being أعوذ ("I seek refuge"); (اللَّه) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the subject (ism) of anna [Translator's note: so in the source («أنّ»); the particle here is إنّ.] [Note: it refers to his master, or it refers to the Creator, Exalted is He, and this is better.. Some said:
the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and (ربي أحسن مثواي) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, this clause being the khabar of inna.], (ربيّ) the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أحسن) a past verb, the fāʿil being "he"; (مثواي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) like the first, and (الهاء) the pronoun of the matter, in the position of accusative as the subject of inna; (لا) negating; (يفلح) an imperfect verb, nominative; (الظالمون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «راودته التي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو في بيتها ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (التي).
The clause «غلّقت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هيت لك» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «(أعوذ) معاذ اللَّه» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «إنّه ربيّ ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أحسن مثواي» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of inna [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (ربّ), its governor being the sense of emphasis contained in inna.].
The clause «إنّه لا يفلح الظالمون» has no grammatical position: a badal (substitute) of the causal clause.
The clause «لا يفلح الظالمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
(الواو) conjunctive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (همت) like راودت; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (همت); (الواو) conjunctive; (همّ) a past verb, the fāʿil being "she" [Translator's note: so in the source («هي»); the fāʿil of همّ is "he", i.e. Yūsuf.]; (بها) like به, attached to (همّ); (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle; (أن) a maṣdar-forming (verbal-noun) particle; (رأى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif, the fāʿil being "he"; (برهان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ربّه) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (كذلك) its i'rab has preceded [Note: in verse (21) of this sūra.], and the prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted verb to be supplied according to the interpretation: "We showed him", or "We protected him", or "We did with him" ... etc. (اللام) for reason (taʿlīl); (نصرف) an imperfect verb, accusative by an understood أن after the lām, the fāʿil being "we", for majesty; (عن) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نصرف); (السوء) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفحشاء) conjoined to السوء by the wāw, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن رأى) is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, the khabar being omitted, its implied form being "existent".. and the answer of لولا is omitted, explained by the speech before it, i.e.: "had he not seen ...
he would have inclined to her" [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said in the book al-Baḥr: «The exegetes have dwelt at length on the explanation of these two inclinations (hamm), and some of them ascribed to Yūsuf what may not be ascribed even to individual sinners. What I choose is that no inclination towards her occurred from Yūsuf, upon him be peace, at all; rather it is negated because of seeing the proof, just as you say: "You would have committed a sin had Allah not protected you" ... We say: the answer of لولا is omitted because what precedes indicates it.. so here the implied wording is "had he not seen the proof of his Lord he would have inclined to her"; the seeing of the proof occurred, so the inclination was negated ...» — end of quotation, summarized.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نصرف..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to the omitted verb to which كذلك is attached.
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, the subject of inna; (من عبادنا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of inna.. and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (المخلصين) naʿt (adjective) of عباد, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «همت به ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «همّ بها» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer of the oath [Note: the clause may be resumptive if the pause comes at (همت به).].
The nominal clause «لولا رؤية البرهان» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «رأى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «نصرف ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the understood particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّه من عبادنا ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
(الواو) conjunctive; (استبقا) a past verb.. and (الألف) a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil; (الباب) accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to the door" [Note: or it is a direct object if استبق is made to carry the meaning of بادر ("hasten to").], (الواو) conjunctive; (قدّت) like راودت; (قميصه) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (من دبر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قدّت); (الواو) conjunctive; (ألفيا) like استبقا; (سيدها) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi; (لدى) an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of accusative, attached to an omitted second direct object, i.e. "present at the door"; (الباب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (قالت) like راودت; (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (جزاء) khabar, nominative; (من) a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (أراد) a past verb, the fāʿil being "he", and it is the returning pronoun; (بأهلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of (سوءا).. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi; (سوءا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (يسجن) a passive imperfect verb, accusative, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يسجن..) is in the position of nominative as a badal of جزاء.
(أو) a conjunction; (عذاب) conjoined to the position of the interpreted maṣdar, nominative like it; (أليم) naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «استبقا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer of the implied oath.
The clause «قدّت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause استبقا الباب.
The clause «ألفيا..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause استبقا الباب.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «ما جزاء ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أراد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «يسجن» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
(قال) a past verb, the fāʿil being "he"; (هي) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (راودت) like the first, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) an object pronoun, the fāʿil being "she"; (عن نفسي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (راودت), and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (شهد) a past verb; (شاهد) fāʿil, nominative; (من أهلها) a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective (naʿt) of شاهد.. and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi; (إن) a conditional particle making jussive; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator — in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (قميصه) the subject of kāna, nominative.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (قدّ) a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (it); (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قدّ); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (صدقت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine [Note: the past verb is joined with the fāʾ because it is past in form and meaning, and for this reason (قد) is implied with it, so that the past is brought close to the present.], (الواو) conjunctive; (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (من الكاذبين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «هي راودتني ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «راودتني ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هي.
The clause «شهد شاهد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال..
The clause «كان قميصه قدّ ...» has no grammatical position: it explains the testimony [Note: because شهد carries the meaning of speaking without its letters.. The clause may also be the maqūl al-qawl of an implied verb of saying, i.e. "a witness testified, saying".].
The clause «قدّ من قبل» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of kāna.
The clause «(قد) صدقت ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هو من الكاذبين» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
(الواو) conjunctive; (إن كان ... وهو من الصادقين) like its counterpart, in single words and clauses.
(الفاء) conjunctive; (لما رأى قميصه) like لما بلغ أشدّه [Note: in verse (22) of this sūra.], (قدّ من دبر) like قدّ من قبل; (قال) as before; (إنّه من كيدكنّ) like إنّه من عبادنا; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (كيدكنّ) its subject, accusative.. and (كنّ) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.. and (النون) with shadda is the sign of the feminine plural; (عظيم) khabar, nominative.
The clause «رأى قميصه ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قدّ من دبر ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl with an implied (قد).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «إنّه من كيدكنّ» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «إنّ كيدكنّ عظيم» has no grammatical position: it has the status of a causal clause.
(يوسف) the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun with the vocative particle omitted, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative; (أعرض) an imperative verb, the fāʿil being "you"; (عن) a preposition; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (أعرض); (الواو) conjunctive; (استغفري) like أكرمي [Note: in verse (21) of this sūra.], (لذنبك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استغفري) [Note: i.e. "seek forgiveness on account of this sin", so the lām is causal.].. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّك) a particle resembling the verb..
and (الكاف) the subject of inna; (كنت) an incomplete past verb.. and (التاء) a pronoun, the subject of kāna; (من الخاطئين) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of kāna. The vocative clause «يوسف ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech [Note: it may be in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl of an implied verb of saying.].
The clause «أعرض ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «استغفري ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّك كنت ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «كنت من الخاطئين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(هيت): there is disagreement over the derivation of this word. Some made the tāʾ radical, the word being a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the past or of the imperative; others made the tāʾ the nominative pronoun, attached to a verb هاء يهيء like جاء يجيء, or هاء يهاء like شاء يشاء, the hamza having been lightened into a quiescent yāʾ according to the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz ... etc.
(معاذ): a mīmī maṣdar from عاذ يعوذ; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn..
It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution, because the alif was originally a wāw; its original form is معوذ with fatḥa on the mīm and the wāw; when the wāw came voweled after a fatḥa it was changed into an alif.
(المخلصين): plural of المخلص, passive participle from the quadriliteral أخلصهم اللَّه, i.e. "Allah chose them and selected them"; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(لدى): an adverbial noun containing iʿlāl: the yāʾ was changed into an alif because it came after a fatḥa, and the yāʾ returns when the adverb is annexed to a pronoun.
(قبل): a noun, the opposite of الدبر ("the back"), taken from قبل قبلا, i.e. "it came forward and drew near"; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas, and it may be pronounced with sukūn on the bāʾ.
(الخاطئين): plural of الخاطئ, active participle from خطئ يخطأ of the فرح class; its pattern is فاعل, its feminine خاطئة.

* Rhetoric:
1- Confirming the purpose for which the speech is driven: this is in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَراوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ». The relative clause is brought, rather than "the wife of the ʿAzīz", although that would be shorter and clearer, in order to confirm the seduction, since his being in her house is something that invites to it — one woman was asked: "What led you to the state you are in, in which there is no good?" She said: "Nearness of the pillow and length of companionship" — and to show the perfection of his chastity, upon him be peace; for his not inclining to her despite his constant beholding of her charms, and his resisting her despite being under her hand, proclaims that he, upon him be peace, was at the highest stations of chastity.
2- The words of Allah the Exalted «هِيَ راوَدَتْنِي»: «هي» is a pronoun by agreement, and it is not for an absent person but for one who is present; likewise (يا أَبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ); this one is with the attached pronoun and that one with the detached.
Al-Sirāj al-Bulqīnī said in his treatise entitled «Nashr al-ʿAbīr li-Ṭayy al-Ḍamīr»:
The element explaining the third-person pronoun is either stated explicitly, or dispensed with by the presence of what it refers to, perceptibly or in knowledge. The perceptible [Translator's note: the source has «فالحسن», evidently for «فالحسّي», "the perceptible".] is as in the words of Allah the Exalted «هِيَ راوَدَتْنِي» and «يا أَبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ», as Ibn Mālik mentioned; and he (al-Bulqīnī) objected to him that it is not as he exemplified it, because these two pronouns refer back to what precedes them: the pronoun of «هِيَ راوَدَتْنِي» refers to "the family" in her words (ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا), and since she alluded to herself with that and did not say بي ("against me") instead of (بأهلك), he, upon him be peace, alluded to her with the third-person pronoun and said (هِيَ راوَدَتْنِي), and did not address her with "you seduced me", nor point to her with "this one seduced me". All of this is by way of courtesy in words and modesty in address befitting the prophets, upon them be peace; so he presented the noun in the form of a third-person pronoun out of courtesy towards the ʿAzīz and modesty before him. And the pronoun of (استأجره) refers to Mūsā, so what explains it is stated explicitly in its wording. It is as though Ibn Mālik imagined that this was a place for pointing, since the owner of the pronoun was present with the one addressed, and so believed that the explaining element is dispensed with by the perceptible presence of what it refers to, so the pronoun was treated like a demonstrative.

* Benefits:
1- The infallibility (ʿiṣma) of the prophets:
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِها لَوْلا أَنْ رَأى بُرْهانَ رَبِّهِ. The sayings of the exegetes concerning this verse are many. We shall present those closest to the truth, if Allah the Exalted wills, since it is the source of questioning for many.
1- ولقد همّت به وهمّ بها: some of the verifying scholars said: inclination (hamm) is of two kinds. A settled inclination, which is that accompanied by resolve, intention, conviction and consent, like the inclination of the wife of the ʿAzīz; the servant is taken to account for it and reckoned for it, as evidenced by the words of Allah the Exalted وَراوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَغَلَّقَتِ الْأَبْوابَ وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ. The second inclination is the passing inclination, which is a thought occurring in the heart and the talk of the self without choice or resolve, like the inclination of Yūsuf, upon him blessings and peace; the servant is not taken to account for it so long as he does not speak of it or act on it. The evidence that Yūsuf, upon him blessings and peace, was neither resolved upon nor consenting to the indecency is the words of Allah the Exalted قالَ مَعاذَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ رَبِّي أَحْسَنَ مَثْوايَ إِنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ.
2- لَوْلا أَنْ رَأى بُرْهانَ رَبِّهِ: the exegetes have many sayings on this matter, and we shall quote the most important of them:
1- Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq said: the proof is the prophethood which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed in his heart; it stood between him and what angers Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
2- The proof is the argument of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, against the servant in the prohibition of fornication, and the knowledge of the punishment due upon the fornicator.
3- Allah, Mighty and Majestic, purified the souls of the prophets, upon them blessings and peace, from blameworthy traits and base deeds, and created them with noble, pure traits which restrain them from doing what is unbefitting, make sinfulness and disobedience hateful to them, and adorn faith and obedience in their hearts, as evidenced by the words of Allah the Exalted كَذلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ السُّوءَ وَالْفَحْشاءَ إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبادِنَا الْمُخْلَصِينَ.
2- Omission of the vocative particle:
The grammarians said: it is permissible to omit the vocative particle and imply it. This occurs in the noble verse in the words of Allah the Exalted يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هذا, and in other verses, such as the words of Allah the Exalted رَبَّنا لا تُؤاخِذْنا إِنْ نَسِينا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنا, i.e. "O our Lord". This is frequent and widespread in the styles of the Arabs. The omitted, implied vocative particle is (يا), because it is the best-known of the vocative particles, and the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not called upon except with it.
If (يا) is followed by something that is not a munādā (the one addressed), such as a verb (ألا يا اسجدوا), or a particle, as in the words of Allah the Exalted (يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً, and their saying يا ربّ كاسية في الدنيا عارية يوم القيامة ("many a woman clothed in this world will be naked on the Day of Resurrection"), or a nominal clause, as in the words of the poet:
يا لعنة الله والأقوام كلهم ... والصالحين على سمعان من جار
(The curse of Allah and of all peoples and of the righteous be upon Simʿān as a neighbour!)
— then it has been said that (يا) in the foregoing is for the vocative with the one addressed omitted, and it has been said that it is for mere alerting, so that the excess of omitting the whole clause is not entailed. This is the correct view, and Allah the Exalted knows best. Ibn Mālik said: if it is followed by a supplication, as in the previous verse of poetry, or a command, as in our saying (ألا يا اسجدوا), then it is for the vocative, because the vocative frequently occurs before supplication and command, as in the words of Allah the Exalted يا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ, يا نُوحُ اهْبِطْ and وَنادَوْا يا مالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنا رَبُّكَ; otherwise it is for alerting.

safi-cedvel:30-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (قال) past verb; (نسوة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (في المدينة) preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of نسوة; (امرأة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (العزيز) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (تراود) imperfect verb, nominative; (فتاها) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif.. and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi; (عن نفسه) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تراود).. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq); (شغفها) past verb.. and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "he"; (حبّا) tamyīz (specification), accusative, transferred from the agent; (إنّا) its i'rab has passed [Note: in āya (17) of this sūra.]; (اللام) for emphasis; (نراها) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif.. and (ها) mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "we"; (في ضلال) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; (مبين) naʿt of ضلال, genitive.
The clause «قال نسوة ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «امرأة العزيز تراود ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تراود فتاها ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «قد شغفها ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya) [Note: or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the agent of تراود or from its object.].
The clause «إنّا لنراها ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نراها ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
(الفاء) conjunction; (لما) an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna) carrying the sense of a condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (أرسلت); (سمعت) past verb.. and (التاء) for the feminine, and the agent is "she"; (بمكر) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سمعت); (هنّ) an attached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (أرسلت) like سمعت; (إلى) preposition and (هن) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أرسلت); (الواو) conjunction; (أعتدت) like سمعت; (لهنّ) like إليهنّ, attached to (أعتدت); (متّكأ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (آتت) like سمعت; (كلّ) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (واحدة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (منهنّ) like إليهنّ, attached to a naʿt of كلّ واحدة; (سكّينا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (قالت) like سمعت; (اخرج) imperative verb, and the agent is "you"; (عليهنّ) like إليهنّ, attached to a ḥāl from the agent of اخرج [Note: or attached to the verb اخرج, and the meaning of اخرج عليهنّ is: come out before them / appear to them.]; (فلما) like the first; (رأين) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (النون) a pronoun, the agent, and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi; (أكبرنه) like رأينه; (الواو) conjunction; (قطّعن) like رأين; (أيدي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هنّ) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (قلن) like رأين; (حاش) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif that was dropped for lightening, and the agent is "he", i.e. Yūsuf; (لله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of حاش, i.e. "obedient to Allah" [Note: or the lām is causal, and it is attached to the verb, on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. Yūsuf kept apart from disobedience for the sake of obedience to Allah.]; (ما) a negative particle operating like laysa; (ها) particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the noun of mā; (بشرا) the predicate of mā, accusative; (إنّ) negative particle [Translator's note: the source writes it with a shadda (إنّ); the negative particle is إنْ]; (هذا) mubtadaʾ; (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ملك) khabar, nominative; (كريم) naʿt of ملك, nominative.
The clause «سمعت ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أرسلت ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أعتدت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «آتت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «اخرج عليهنّ» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «رأينه ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أكبرنه ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قطّعن ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أكبرنه.
The clause «قلن ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أكبرنه.
The clause «حاش لله» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying [Note: or it is a parenthetical clause of supplication, and the object of the saying is the clause ما هذا بشرا.].
The clause «ما هذا بشرا ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إن هذا إلّا ملك....» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption of the preceding resumption.

* Morphology:
(نسوة): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own root; its singular is امرأة. It is with kasra on the nūn — they said it may also take ḍamma — and in that case it is a collective noun without dispute.
(العزيز): a title for the minister who was over the treasuries of Egypt, whose name was (قطفير), as reported in the exegeses.
(فتاها): the alif in it is converted from a yāʾ; its plural is فتية and its dual فتيان; its origin is فتي, and when the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa it was changed to alif.
(مكرهنّ): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb مكر يمكر, of the pattern naṣara; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(متّكأ): a noun of place from the five-letter verb اتكأ; in the āya it is used as a noun meaning the cushion, or the food that requires reclining and a knife to cut it ... so it is on the pattern of the passive participle.. In the word there is a substitution of the first radical (fāʾ) by tāʾ because it comes before the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form; its origin is موتكأ.. then the two tāʾs were assimilated together.
(سكّينا): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the cutting instrument; its wazn is فعّيل, with kasra on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn.
(حاشى): it is a four-letter verb whose imperfect is يحاشي; the short form of the alif in its spelling is because it is the fourth letter. When it is a preposition, the alif is written tall (حاشا). Others hold it is a noun meaning "in exaltation / far be it" (tanzīhan), since its end takes tanwīn; the tanwīn may be dropped for necessity, i.e. حاشا with tanwīn and حاشا without tanwīn. (كريم): a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the active participle) from كرم يكرم; its wazn is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ما هذا بَشَراً إِنْ هذا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ» the women likened Yūsuf to an angel without mentioning the particle of comparison. Its purpose is to affirm beauty, because Allah the Exalted placed in natures that nothing is more beautiful than an angel — and the people of Lūṭ witnessed that in the guests of Ibrāhīm among the angels — just as He placed in natures that nothing is uglier than the devil, as in His saying describing Hell «طَلْعُها كَأَنَّهُ رُؤُسُ الشَّياطِينِ». So likewise it is established that nothing is more beautiful than an angel, and when the women wanted to describe Yūsuf as beautiful they likened him to an angel. But the Quranic style chose to go beyond the familiar similes of the Arabs, who likened every human whose beauty amazed them to the jinn, and it brought in another device that does not appear to the onlooker at first glance: a device they defined as the speaker asking about something he truly knows, feigning ignorance of it,
so that his speech comes out as praise, or to indicate — as here — the intensity of infatuation in love; it may also be intended for blame, wonder, rebuke or affirmation. This device is called tajāhul al-ʿārif (feigned ignorance of the knower).
2- The figurative usage (majāz): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَأً», i.e. the pillows and cushions they recline on,
for the Prophet ﷺ forbade a man to eat with his left hand and to eat reclining.
It is also said that the food itself is meant. Al-ʿUtbī said: one says "we reclined at so-and-so's", meaning we ate; and from that is the saying of Jamīl:
فظللنا بنعمة واتكأنا ... وشربنا الحلال من قلله
(So we spent the day in comfort and reclined [i.e. feasted], and drank the lawful from its jugs.)
It expressed it figuratively by the posture in which the luxurious eater is; and it is said: it belongs to the category of kināya (metonymy).

* Benefits:
- حاشا:
In this āya occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted وَقُلْنَ حاشَ لِلَّهِ ما هذا بَشَراً. Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī says concerning (حاشى) in this noble āya: It is read with two alifs (حاشا). The majority hold that here it is a verb; أحاشي has been conjugated from it. This is supported by the entry of the lām on the name of Allah the Exalted; had it been a preposition, another preposition would not come after it. Its agent is latent, its implied form being (حاشا يوسف), i.e. he kept far from disobedience by the particle of Allah [Translator's note: the source reads «بحرف الله» ("by the particle of Allah"); al-ʿUkbarī's wording is probably «لخوف الله» ("out of fear of Allah"); translated as written]. The origin of the word is from حاشيت الشيء (I set the thing aside). It is also read with the alif dropped for lightening.
This is what Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī stated. To complete the benefit, we will clarify what pertains to (حاشا), because it is obscure to many. حاشا occurs in three ways:
1- That it be a transitive, conjugable verb; you say حاشيته meaning "I excepted him", the evidence being the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī: ولا أرى فاعلا في الناس يشبهه ... ولا أحاشي من الأقوام من أحد (I see no doer among people resembling him, and I except no one of the tribes.)
2- That it be for exaltation (tanzīh), as passed in the noble āya (حاشى لله); it is a noun of exaltation, like the saying of Allah the Exalted مَعاذَ اللَّهِ, and we parse it as a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
3- It occurs for exception; most commonly it is a preposition conveying exception and the noun after it is genitive, as when we say: كلكم مخطئ حاشا زيد (all of you are wrong except Zayd). Some grammarians held another permissible view, namely that we consider it a non-conjugable (jāmid) verb conveying exception, with the noun after it a mafʿūl bihi in the accusative, as in their saying: (اللهم اغفر لي ولمن يسمع حاشا الشيطان) (O Allah, forgive me and whoever hears, except the devil).

safi-cedvel:97-97.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (يا أبانا) its i'rab has already been given «[Note: in verse (81) of this sūra.]»; (استغفر) an imperative verb, the fāʿil being "you" (أنت); (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استغفر); (ذنوبنا) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّا كنّا خاطئين) is like «إن كنّا لخاطئين» «[Note: in verse (91) of this sūra.]».
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يا أبانا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «استغفر ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كنّا خاطئين ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:98-98.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being "he" (هو); (سوف) a particle of the future; (أستغفر) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the fāʿil being "I" (أنا); (لكم) is like (لنا) «[Note: in the previous verse (97).]», attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أستغفر); (ربّي) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّه هو الغفور الرحيم) is like «إنّه هو العليم الحكيم» «[Note: in verse (83) of this sūra.]».
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أستغفر ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّه هو الغفور ...» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «هو الغفور ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:99-100.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آوى); (دخلوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (على يوسف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (دخلوا), its sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (آوى) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (إلى) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to (آوى); (أبويه) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), its sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (قال) a past verb, the fāʿil being "he" (هو), i.e. Yūsuf; (ادخلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) the fāʿil; (مصر) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, prevented from nunation because of being a proper name and feminine; (إن) a particle of condition making the verb jussive; (شاء) a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (آمنين) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, its sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «دخلوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آوى ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ادخلوا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «شاء الله ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya).. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "If Allah wills your entering in safety, you will have entered."
(الواو) a conjunction; (رفع) a past verb, the fāʿil being "he" (هو); (أبويه) is like the first one; (على العرش) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (رفع); (الواو) a conjunction; (خرّوا) is like (دخلوا); (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (خرّوا); (سجّدا) a ḥāl, accusative, from the fāʿil of (خرّوا); (الواو) a conjunction; (قال) is like (رفع); (يا) a vocative particle; (أبت) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the kasra — the kasra of harmony — has been transferred to the tāʾ that substitutes for the yāʾ of the first person..
and (ياء) of the first person, which is omitted, is a pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (تأويل) a khabar (predicate), nominative; (رؤياي) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the implied kasra.. and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من) a preposition; (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (رؤياي) «[Note: or to a ḥāl from الرؤيا, whose governing word (ʿāmil) is the demonstrative.]»; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (جعلها) is like (رفع).. and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (ربّي) a fāʿil, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (حقّا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative «[Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar by being its adjective, i.e. "a true making" (جعلا حقّا).]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (قد أحسن) is like (قد جعل); (بي) is like (له), attached to (أحسن); (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (أحسن); (أخرج) is like (رفع), and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (من السجن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخرجني); (الواو) a conjunction; (جاء) is like (رفع); (بكم) is like (له), attached to (جاء); (من البدو) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء); (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء); (أن) a maṣdar particle; (نزغ) is like (رفع); (الشيطان) a fāʿil, nominative; (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (نزغ), its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ ... and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi «[Translator's note: so in the source; in the text «بيني» the fatḥa of بين is overt.]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (بين) is like the first one and is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; (إخوتي) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the letter before the yāʾ ... and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (ربّي) the noun of إنّ, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ ... and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (لطيف) the khabar of إنّ, nominative; and (اللام) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (لطيف) in the sense of "one who arranges" (مدبّر); (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil being "he" (هو).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نزغ..) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (بعد) to it.
(إنّ) is like the first one, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of إنّ; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (العليم) a khabar, nominative; (الحكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «رفع ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied clause following the course of the story, i.e.:
"When Yūsuf entered Egypt he sat upon his throne and raised his parents upon the throne".
The clause «خرّوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «رفع».
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «رفع».
The vocative clause «يا أبت ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya).
The clause «هذا تأويل ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «جعلها ربّي ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, either anticipated (muqaddara) or concurrent (muqārina).
The clause «أحسن بي ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause «جعلها ربّي».. «[Note: it may be cut off as a resumption, and then it has no grammatical position.]».
The clause «أخرجني ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «جاء بكم ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause «أخرجني».
The clause «نزغ الشيطان ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ ربّي لطيف ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption carrying the sense of giving a reason.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّه هو العليم ...» has no grammatical position, being a causal resumption.
The clause «هو العليم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(البدو): a name for open, level land in which a person appears (يبدو) from afar; it has been named with the name of the maṣdar (verbal noun).. It may also be applied to the inhabitants of the desert from among the nomadic tribes.. البدو in the sense of the desert has the plurals باديات and بواد.

* Rhetoric:
1- Synecdoche (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted «وَقالَ ادْخُلُوا مِصْرَ إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ».
It is known that they would not take up the whole country; rather they would enter a part of it. So the whole was expressed while the part was meant, and the relation of this figure is that of the whole (al-kulliyya).

safi-cedvel:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb), with the vocative particle omitted from it, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ that has been omitted for lightness, and (الياء), omitted, is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (آتيت) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (التاء) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent), and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من الملك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آتيتني) «[Note: and (من) is for clarifying the genus.. It may also be partitive — this is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān alone — and then it is attached to an adjective of the implied object, i.e.: "You have given me a great [share] of the dominion" (آتيني عظيما من الملك).]» «[Translator's note: «آتيني» is so written in the source; آتيتني is evidently meant.]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (علّمتني) is like (آتيتني); (من تأويل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (علّمتني) «[Note: or it is partitive like the first, attached to an adjective of the omitted object, i.e.: "You have taught me a portion of the interpretation of events" (علّمتني حظّا من تأويل الأحاديث).]»; (الأحاديث) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (فاطر) a munādā, a muḍāf, accusative, with the vocative particle omitted from it «[Note: or it is a badal (substitute) from (ربّ), or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or a naʿt (adjective) ...]»; (السموات) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (السموات) by the wāw, genitive; (أنت) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (وليّي) a khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (في الدّنيا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (وليّ), its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif; (الآخرة) conjoined to (الدنيا) by the wāw, genitive; (توفّني) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter.. and (النّون) is for protection and (الياء) a mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being "you" (أنت); (مسلما) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (ألحقني) is like (توفّني); (بالصّالحين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ألحق), its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The vocative clause «ربّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آتيتني ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «علّمتني ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The vocative clause «فاطر السموات ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive — or a substitute (badal) for the vocative clause.
The clause «أنت وليّي ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the second vocative.
The clause «توفّني ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the vocative.
The clause «ألحقني ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «توفّني».

safi-cedvel:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Jacob; (يا) a vocative particle; (بنيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, for it is treated like the sound masculine plural, and the second (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (لا) prohibitive, making jussive; (تدخلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من باب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تدخلوا); (واحد) naʿt (adjective) of باب, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (ادخلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (من أبواب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ادخلوا); (متفرّقة) naʿt of أبواب, genitive; (الواو) conjunctive; (ما) negating; (أغني) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "I"; (عن) a preposition; (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أغني); (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of شيء; (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (شيء) genitive in form, accusative in position, a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "I do not avail you any availing" or "anything of availing" [Note: It may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by making أغني carry the meaning of أدفع, i.e. "I do not ward off — or it does not ward off — from you — or from them — anything of the decree."]. (إن) a particle of negation; (الحكم) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (عليه) like عنكم, attached to (توكّلت), which is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn ...
and (التاء) is the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunctive; (عليه) like the first, attached to (يتوكّل); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (يتوكّل) an imperfect verb, jussive; (المتوكّلون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال in the previous verse [Note: Or it is resumptive in the first place.].
The vocative clause «يا بنيّ ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا تدخلوا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «ادخلوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «ما أغني ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «إن الحكم إلّا لله ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «توكّلت ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «يتوكّل المتوكّلون ...» is in the position of jussive: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if judgement belongs to Allah, then let those who rely rely upon Him" ... and the implied conditional clause has no grammatical position: conjoined to the preceding resumption [Note: Or it is resumptive in the first place.].

safi-cedvel:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (لمّا دخلوا) like لمّا رجعوا [Note: In verse (63) of this sūra.]; (من) a preposition; (حيث) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (دخلوا); (أمرهم) a past verb, and (هم) an object pronoun; (أبوهم) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) ... and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ما) negating; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and its subject (ism) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "it", i.e. their entering separately; (يغني) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e. the entering; (عنهم) like عنكم, attached to (يغني); (من الله من شيء) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse (67); see note no. (1) on the previous page.]; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (حاجة) accusative (manṣūb) as an exception of the disjoined kind (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); (في نفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of حاجة; (يعقوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (قضاها) a past verb, and (ها) an object pronoun, and the fāʿil is "he"; (الواو) resumptive; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the subject (ism) of inna; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (ذو) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (علم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (اللام) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the clause being its ṣila (relative clause) and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "for what We taught him."]; (علّمنا) a past verb indeclinable on sukūn ... and (نا) is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) an object pronoun; (الواو) conjunctive; (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for rectification (istidrāk); (أكثر) the subject of lākinna, accusative; (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا) negating; (يعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «دخلوا ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the meaning of the negated clause ما كان يغني عنهم..., i.e. "what befell them befell them" [Note: The clause ما كان يغني cannot be the apodosis, because what follows negating (ما) does not govern what precedes it, and because the apodosis clause governs (لمّا) ... But the clause ما كان يغني may be the apodosis if (لمّا) is parsed as a particle of "existence upon existence" (or "necessity upon existence").].
The clause «ما كان يغني ...» is in the position of accusative: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of دخلوا ..., i.e. "fleeing from the decree of Allah not benefiting them" [Note: The clause may be resumptive if the apodosis is implied.].
The clause «يغني ...» is in the position of accusative: the khabar of kāna.
The clause «قضاها ...» is in the position of accusative: a naʿt of حاجة.
The clause «إنّه لذو علم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «علّمناه ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «لكنّ أكثر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّه لذو علم ...
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of lākinna.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما علّمناه ...) is in the position of genitive governed by the lām, attached to (علم).

* Morphology:
(حاجة): a noun for what one needs; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ; its plurals are حاج and حوج — with kasra on the ḥāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw — and حاجات and حوائج, the last on the assumption of a singular حائجة ... The alif in (حاجة) is changed from a wāw; its original form is حوجة: the wāw came after a fatḥa and was changed to alif.

safi-cedvel:69-69.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (لمّا دخلوا ... آوى) like لمّا رجعوا ...
قالوا [Note: In verse (63) of this sūra.]; (إلى) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آوى); (أخاه) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the alif ... and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Joseph; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the subject (ism) of inna; (أنا) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (أخوك) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw ... and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunctive, linking the effect to the cause; (لا) prohibitive, making jussive; (تبتئس) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil is "you"; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (تبتئس), the returning pronoun being omitted; (كانوا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb ... and (الواو) is the subject of kāna; (يعلمون) like the previous one [Note: In the previous verse (68).] [Translator's note: the verse has يعملون; the source prints يعلمون here, as in verse 68.].
The clause «دخلوا ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آوى ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition [Note: Some make this clause the apodosis of both conditions together.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) with (قد) implied.].
The clause «إنّي أنا أخوك ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنا أخوك ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «لا تبتئس ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "take heed, then do not grieve".
The clause «كانوا يعملون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يعملون ...» is in the position of accusative: the khabar of kānū.

* Morphology:
[آوى): the alif in it is changed from a yāʾ — iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution: the yāʾ, being vowelled, came after a fatḥa and was changed to alif. The madda consists of a hamza followed by a second alif, so it is on the pattern فاعل; its imperfect is يؤاوى.. See verse (72) of sūrat al-Anfāl.

safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunctive; (لمّا جهّزهم ... جعل) the i'rab of its parallel has already been given [Note: In verse (63) of this sūra.]; (السقاية) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (في رحل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جعل); (أخيه) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) ... and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (أذّن) a past verb; (مؤذّن) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (أيّتها) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of accusative ... (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (العير) badal (substitute) of أيّة — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — nominative in form; (إنّكم) like إنّي [Note: In the previous verse (69).]; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (سارقون) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «جهّزهم ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أذّن مؤذّن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «أيّتها العير ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «إنّكم لسارقون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the call.

* Morphology:
(السقاية): a primitive (jāmid) noun for the vessel from which one gives drink; its pattern is فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ ... See verse (19) of al-Tawba.
(العير): a noun for every animal on which loads are carried — camels, donkeys and mules — and here the owners of the camels are meant ... In al-Miṣbāḥ: al-ʿīr, with kasra, is originally a name for the camels that carry provisions; then it came to be used predominantly for any caravan.

* Rhetoric:
- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope): in the words of Allah the Exalted «أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسارِقُونَ»; its relation is adjacency, and what is meant here is the owners of the caravan, as in
the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «يا خيل الله اركبي» ("O horses of Allah, mount!").

* Benefits:
- «ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ»:
That is: it is used as a means to address what is made definite by al-; it is a noun indeclinable on ḍamma. Its parallel has already come up with us, where a detailed treatment of this discussion was called for, so return to it where detail is required.
And العير is a badal (substitute) of the one addressed.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (أقبلوا) like قالوا; (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقبلوا); (ماذا) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ذا) a relative noun, the khabar (predicate), the clause تفقدون being the ṣila (relative clause) with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. تفقدونه; and the clause ماذا is the speech reported.]; (تفقدون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ...
and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أقبلوا ...» is in the position of accusative: a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.
The clause «تفقدون ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).

safi-cedvel:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (نفقد) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is "we"; (صواع) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الملك) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (اللام) a preposition; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); (جاء) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he", which is the returning pronoun; (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (جاء); (حمل) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (بعير) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) resumptive; (أنا زعيم) like أنا أخوك [Note: In verse (69) of this sūra.]; (به) like the first, attached to (زعيم).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نفقد ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لمن جاء ... حمل» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the speech reported.
The clause «جاء به ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «أنا به زعيم ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported of an implied verb of saying, i.e. "and the caller said: I am guarantor for it" ... and the implied clause of saying is resumptive,

* Morphology:
(صواع): a noun for the measuring vessel; it is the drinking-cup (السقاية) mentioned in the previous verse. The word صواع is treated as both masculine and feminine; its pattern is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ, on the measure of غراب.
(زعيم): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from زعم يزعم, of the فتح class and the نصر class, i.e. "he stood surety for it"; its pattern is فعيل; its plural is زعماء, on the measure فعلاء with ḍamma on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:73-73.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (التاء) the tāʾ of oath; (الله) the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) by the tāʾ of oath, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear"; (اللام) the lām of oath; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (علمتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn ... and (تم) a pronoun, the fāʿil; (ما) negating; (جئنا) like علمتم; (اللام) the lām of cause (taʿlīl); (نفسد) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the fāʿil is "we"; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نفسد); (الواو) conjunctive; (ما) negating; (كنّا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and its subject (ism); (سارقين) the khabar (predicate) of kunnā, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «(نقسم) بالله ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قد علمتم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.
The clause «ما جئنا ...» is in the position of accusative: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of knowing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the negation.
The clause «نفسد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن نفسد) is in the position of genitive governed by the lām, attached to (جئنا).
The clause «ما كنا سارقين ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause (ما) جئنا.

safi-cedvel:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (جزاؤه) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) ... and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إن) a conditional particle making jussive; (كنتم) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) a pronoun, the subject (ism) of kāna; (كاذبين) the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما جزاؤه ...» is in the position of jussive: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if he is a thief and you are lying, then what is his recompense?" .. and the implied conditional clause is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كنتم كاذبين ...» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the first implied condition ...
And the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the (ما) before it, i.e. "if you are lying, then what is his recompense".

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(قالت) past verb, and (التاء) for the feminine, and the agent is "she"; (الفاء) linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (ذلكنّ) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) for distance, and (كنّ) a particle of address for the feminine plural; (الذي) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (لمتنّ) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تنّ) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (النون) the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya); (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لمتنّ), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "in love of him" [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of لمتنّ, i.e. you blamed me while I was infatuated in love of him.]; (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath for an implied oath; (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq); (راودت) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء) agent and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (عن نفسه) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (راودته).. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) conjunction; (استعصم) past verb, and the agent is "he"; (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) preparing for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (إن) jussive conditional particle; (لم) negative particle; (يفعل) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the agent is "he"; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (آمره) imperfect verb, nominative, and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "I"; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يسجننّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative..
and (النون) the nūn of emphasis; it is passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he); (الواو) conjunction; (ليكوننّ) the lām of the oath and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, like يسجننّ in being indeclinable, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he); (من الصاغرين) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the predicate of يكونن.
The clause «قالت» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ذلكنّ الذي» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have blamed me, then that is the one about whom you blamed me".. and the clause of condition and apodosis is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لمتنّني ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «راودته» has no grammatical position, the answer to an implied oath.. and the oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
The clause «استعصم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer of the oath.
The clause «إن لم يفعل ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمره» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما), and the referring pronoun is omitted.
The clause «يسجننّ» has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «يكونن من الصاغرين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(لمتنّ): it contains a weakness change by deletion (iʿlāl bil-ḥadhf) to suit being indeclinable on the sukūn; it is a hollow (ajwaf) weak verb whose middle radical (ʿayn) was deleted for that reason; its wazn is فلتنّ.

* Rhetoric:
Ellipsis (al-ḥadhf): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «فَذلِكُنَّ الَّذِي لُمْتُنَّنِي فِيهِ», the implied form being "in love of him", because blame does not attach to persons themselves. The evidence for implying "in love of him" is His saying «قَدْ شَغَفَها حُبًّا»; [or it is] "in seducing him", and perhaps this is more fitting, given His saying «تُراوِدُ فَتاها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ». We said "more fitting" only because it is her act, unlike love, which is a compelling matter for which one is not blamed except in respect of pursuing its causes. As for seduction, it occurs by her own acquisition, so she is able to repel it, and thus blame can attach to it — unlike love, for it is not her act and she cannot repel it, since excessive love may overpower its owner and he cannot bear to repel it, and then he is not blamed for it. In any case, it [the seduction] is one of its causes.

safi-cedvel:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) past verb, and the agent is "he", i.e. Yūsuf; (ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb), its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ that was dropped for lightening.. and the dropped (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (السجن) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (أحبّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (إلى) preposition and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحبّ; (من) preposition; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to أحبّ; (يدعون) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (النون) the nūn of the feminine plural, the fāʿil (agent), and the second (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إليه) like إليّ, attached to (يدعون); (الواو) conjunction; (إن) jussive conditional particle; (لا) negative particle; (تصرف) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (عنّي) like إليّ, attached to (تصرف); (كيدهنّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (هنّ) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أصب) imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "I"; (إليهنّ) like إليّ, attached to (أصب); (الواو) conjunction; (أكن) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (أصب), and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I); (من الجاهلين) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted predicate of أكن.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The vocative clause «ربّ ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «السجن أحبّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يدعونني إليه» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «إلّا تصرف عنّي ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object of the saying.
The clause «أصب إليهنّ ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis not joined by fāʾ.
The clause «أكن من الجاهلين» has no grammatical position, an apodosis conjoined to the clause أصب.
(الفاء) conjunction; (استجاب) past verb; (اللام) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (استجاب); (ربّه) agent, nominative.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction; (صرف) like استجاب, and the agent is "he"; (عنه) like له, attached to (صرف); (كيدهنّ) like the first; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; (هو) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose predicate is (السميع), and the nominal clause is the predicate of inna.]; (السميع) the predicate of inna, nominative; (العليم) a second predicate, nominative.
The clause «استجاب له ربّه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قال.
The clause «صرف عنه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استجاب..
The clause «إنّه.. السميع ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
(ثمّ) conjunction; (بدا) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif, and the agent is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech in His saying (السجن أحبّ), the implied form being: "it appeared to them that they should imprison him" [Note: it is permissible that the agent be the maṣdar of the verb بدا, i.e. "a notion (badāʾ) appeared to them", as one says: "an opinion appeared to me".]..; (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (بدا); (من بعد) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (بدا); (ما) maṣdar-forming particle; (رأوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and the wāw is the agent; (الآيات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما رأوا..) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(اللام) the lām of the oath for an implied oath; (يسجننّ) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn — it was dropped because of the succession of identical letters — and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters — the wāw and the [first] nūn of the doubled one — is the agent.. and the doubled (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (حتّى) preposition; (حين) genitive by the preposition, attached to (يسجننّه).
The clause «بدا لهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause صرف..
The clause «رأوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يسجننّه» has no grammatical position, the answer to an implied oath.. and the oath clause with its answer is in the position of accusative, governed by an implied saying which is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the third-person pronoun in لهم, i.e. "it appeared to them that they should imprison him, saying: by Allah, we shall surely imprison him for a time" [Note: it is permissible that the oath clause and its answer be an explication of what precedes it, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(السجن): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the place designated for the restriction of freedom; its wazn is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.. With fatḥa on the sīn it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
(أصب): it contains a weakness change by deletion (iʿlāl bil-ḥadhf) to suit the jussive; its origin is أصبو; its wazn is أفع.

* Benefits:
Can a clause occur as fāʿil (agent), nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) or mubtadaʾ? This is a point of dispute among the grammarians. We will quote what Ibn Hishām mentioned in al-Mughnī on this matter.
The saying of Allah the Exalted ثُمَّ بَدا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما رَأَوُا الْآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّى حِينٍ: the clause ليسجننه — it has been said that it explicates the pronoun in بدا, which refers back to the badāʾ understood from it, the implied form being: "then the notion appeared to them — the notion of imprisoning him". The verified view is that it is the answer to an implied oath, and that the implied oath with its answer is the explicative clause. The Kufans said the clause (ليسجننه) is the agent; then Hishām, Thaʿlab and a group said: that is permissible in every clause; while al-Farrāʾ and a group said: its permissibility is conditional on the verb of the preceding clause being a verb of the heart, and on the clause occurring as agent being joined with a suspending particle, as in: ظهر لي أقام زيد (it became clear to me whether Zayd stood), and علم هل قعد عمرو (it became known whether ʿAmr sat). Ibn Hishām says, commenting on that: Further, in my view the matter is sound, but only with interrogation, not the other suspending particles. And regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ, Ibn ʿUṣfūr claimed that the Basrans take the deputy agent of قيل to be the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. "and when a saying is said to them", with the clause لا تفسدوا explicating that pronoun. What is correct is that the deputy agent is the clause (لا تفسدوا), because before the agent was omitted it was in the accusative governed by the saying, so how would it turn into an explicative? And the object is what substitutes for the agent. Their saying "a clause is not an agent nor a substitute for it" is answered thus: the clause whose wording itself is intended is given the ruling of single words; for this reason it also occurs in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, in his saying, upon him be blessing and peace: «لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله كنز من كنوز الجنة» ("There is no might nor power except by Allah" is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise), and in the proverb «زعموا مطية الكذب» ("They claimed" is the mount of lying). So the clause (لا حول ولا قوة إلا با لله) is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
Hence the predicate did not need a linking element in the likes of «قولي لا إله إلا الله» (my saying is: there is no god but Allah).

safi-cedvel:102-104.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the reference is to what has been mentioned of the story of Yūsuf, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (من أنباء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (الغيب) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (نوحيه) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being "We" (نحن), for majesty; (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نوحيه); (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation; (كنت) a deficient past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (التاء) a pronoun, the noun of kāna; (لدى) an adverb of place, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to the khabar of (كنت).. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of the accusative, attached to the omitted khabar; (أجمعوا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (أمرهم) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb).. and (هم) is like the last one; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يمكرون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) the fāʿil.
The clause «ذلك من أنباء ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «نوحيه ...» is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك) «[Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its governing word being the demonstrative.]».
The clause «ما كنت لديهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أجمعوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «هم يمكرون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «يمكرون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
