(الواو) a conjunction; (ما) negative, working as laysa works; (أكثر) the noun of mā, nominative; (الناس) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) «[Note: it may be circumstantial, and the clause after it a ḥāl.]»; (لو) a non-jussive particle of condition; (حرصت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء) the fāʿil; (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (مؤمنين) the khabar of mā, accusative in position and genitive in form, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «ما أكثر ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «ما كنت لديهم».
The clause «حرصت ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you were eager for the faith of most people, still they are not believers".
(الواو) a conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation; (تسألهم) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being "you" (أنت); (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl from (أجر); (من) a redundant preposition; (أجر) genitive in form, accusative in position, a mafʿūl bihi; (إن) a particle of negation; (هو) is like (هم); (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (ذكر) a khabar, nominative; (للعالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ذكر) «[Note: or attached to an adjective of (ذكر).]».
The clause «ما تسألهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «ما أكثر الناس ...».
The clause «إن هو إلّا ذكر ...» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
1- The art of theoretical argumentation (al-iḥtijāj al-naẓarī):
In the verse there is a subtle art, called in the science of eloquence (ʿilm al-bayān) theoretical argumentation, and some call it the dialectical method (al-madhhab al-kalāmī). It consists in binding the opponent to what necessarily follows from this argument. The meaning is that this news is unseen; you knew it only through revelation, because you were not present with the brothers of Yūsuf, peace be upon him, when they resolved upon what they intended — to put him in the depths of the well — while they were plotting against him; and it is known, and not hidden from those who deny you, that you never met anyone who heard that so that you could have learned it from him. Some of the verifying scholars said: this is mockery of those who denied him, in that the Exalted made the matter in doubt to be his, peace be upon him, being present before the sons of Yaʿqūb, peace be upon him, as they plotted, and so He negated it with His saying «وَما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ».
2- The art of parenthesis (al-iʿtirāḍ): in verse 103. Parenthesis is divided into two kinds: one of them comes in speech only for a benefit, and it runs in the course of emphasis; the other comes in speech for no benefit, and then either its entering it is like its leaving it, or it causes a defect in its composition and a corruption in its meaning. The first kind is like this verse, and the benefit of the parenthesis lies in two respects. The first of them: depicting his ﷺ eagerness for the faith of his people and their guidance, his intense striving to restrain them from their error and to turn them away from the places of mistake and the abodes of misguidance, and his exposing himself to harm for the sake of this eagerness, despite his knowing that this was of no avail and that it was impossible for them to give up what they were in. The second respect: depicting their obstinacy, the stubborn denial of their mentality, and their persistence in the error upon which they had embarked and to which they held. The Noble Qur'an is full of this kind.

* Benefits:
- «وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ»: a parenthetical clause.
Parenthesis is one of the arts of rhetoric, and at the same time a subject the grammarians attend to and whose positions they define. Therefore we shall present its positions to you briefly:
1- Between the verb and its fāʿil.
2- Between the verb and its mafʿūl.
3- Between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar.
4- Between what was originally a mubtadaʾ and khabar, as in the saying of the poet:
إن الثمانين وبلغتها ... أحوجت سمعي الى ترجمان
(Eighty years — and you have reached them — have made my hearing need an interpreter.)
5- Between the condition and its apodosis.
6- Between the oath and its answer.
7- Between the qualified noun and its adjective.
8- Between the relative and its ṣila.
9- Between the particle of futurity (taswīf) and the verb.
10- Between the particle of negation and what it negates.
These are the places in which parenthesis occurs by way of preponderance, not by way of exhaustiveness.
Whoever wishes for a full survey should consult the comprehensive books of grammar that undertake induction and thorough investigation.

safi-cedvel:105-107.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (كأيّن) a noun of allusion (kināya) to a number, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (من آية) a preposition and its genitive noun, the tamyīz (specification) of the kināya; (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of (آية); (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (السموات) by the wāw, genitive (majrūr); (يمرّون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الواو) the fāʿil (agent); (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يمرّون); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ; (عنها) is like (عليها), attached to (معرضون), which is the khabar (predicate), nominative, its sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «كأيّن من آية ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يمرّون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كأيّن).
The clause «هم عنها معرضون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(الواو) a conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation; (يؤمن) an imperfect verb, nominative; (أكثرهم) a fāʿil, nominative.. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمن); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (وهم مشركون) is like (وهم معرضون).
The clause «ما يؤمن أكثرهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause.
The clause «هم مشركون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
(الهمزة) for interrogation; (الفاء) a conjunction «[Note: or resumptive, and the clause after it is resumed.]»; (آمنوا) a past verb and its fāʿil «[Translator's note: so written in the source; the Quranic word is أمنوا (from أَمِنَ), as the source itself writes it below.]»; (أن) a maṣdar particle making the verb accusative; (تأتي) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (غاشية) a fāʿil, nominative; (من عذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt of (غاشية); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; (أو) a conjunction; (تأتيهم الساعة) is like (تأتيهم غاشية) and is conjoined to it; (بغتة) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, accusative; (وهم لا يشعرون) is like (وهم يمكرون).. in verse (102), and (لا) is negative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأتيهم ...) is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being (أمنوا).
The clause «أمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «ما يؤمن أكثرهم».
The clause «تأتيهم غاشية ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تأتيهم الساعة ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «تأتيهم غاشية».
The clause «هم لا يشعرون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يشعرون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(غاشية): the feminine of غاش, an active participle from the triliteral غشي; its pattern is فاعل and its feminine فاعلة, and (الياء) is radical.

* Benefits:
- There is no poetry in the Qur'an:
The Qur'an sometimes aims at musical harmony in its composition, and we have drawn attention to this characteristic in earlier places.
This characteristic was noticed by great scholars and men of letters, among them al-Farrāʾ, al-Jāḥiẓ and Ibn Qutayba.
Al-Jāḥiẓ holds that the Revelation gave the wording special care, choosing it precisely so as to indicate the meanings precisely.
He also dealt with the melody, music and particular regular metre on which the composition of the Qur'an runs, made up of interlinked, harmonious units, and he spent much effort to deny the metre of poetry to the Qur'an.
Someone claimed that the saying of the Exalted «تَبَّتْ يَدا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ» is poetry, and produced its metre in metrical feet. Al-Jāḥiẓ answered him, saying: if you were to examine people's conversations, sermons and letters, you would find that much of them contains many metrical feet, and yet we have no right to call it poetry, since its author did not intend poetry by it..
Ibn Qutayba holds, in his book «Mushkil al-Qurʾān», that the musical melody, the composition and the inner rhythm in the verses are one of the characteristics on which the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Qur'an rests. He says: "He made it recited however long the recitation, heard without the ears rejecting it, and fresh, not wearing out however often it is repeated."
2- The stories of the Qur'an:
As for the Qur'an's way of presenting a story, it has many forms, all of which do not depart from concision and inimitability.
It may narrate the story from its beginning to its end, as came in the story of Yūsuf; and it may return and fold it up after unfolding it, as we saw at the end of this same sūra.
It may present one side of it in one sūra and the other side in another sūra, and it may present it once at length and once briefly; and in all cases it observes the place of the lesson, what the situation requires, and the purpose of the story.

safi-cedvel:108-109.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, the fāʿil (agent) being "you" (أنت); (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذه) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (سبيلي) a khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أدعو) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on (الواو), the fāʿil being "I" (أنا); (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أدعو); (على بصيرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of (أدعو) «[Note: or attached to (أدعو).. or it is a fronted khabar and (أنا) a postponed mubtadaʾ.]», i.e. "being certain"; (أنا) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil of (أدعو); (الواو) a conjunction; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the latent (mustatir) pronoun that is the fāʿil of (أدعو) «[Note: or conjoined to the postponed mubtadaʾ (أنا) ... It may also be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "a caller to Allah upon insight"..]»; (اتّبعني) a past verb, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil being "he" (هو), and it is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid); (الواو) a conjunction; (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "I glorify" (أسبح); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation working as laysa works «[Note: or inoperative.. and (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ and (من المشركين) its khabar.]»; (أنا) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as the noun of mā; (من المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of mā, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هذه سبيلي ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أدعوا إلى الله ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «[Note: or an explication of the preceding saying.]».
The clause «اتّبعني ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «(أسبح) سبحان ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying.
The clause «ما أنا من المشركين ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying.
(الواو) a conjunction; (ما) is like the first one, and it has no governing effect; (أرسلنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil; (من قبلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أرسلنا).. and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (رجالا) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (نوحي) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, the fāʿil being "We" (نحن), for majesty; (إلى) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نوحي); (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (رجالا); (القرى) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (الفاء) a conjunction; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (يسيروا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) the fāʿil; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسيروا) «[Note: or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of (يسيروا).]»; (الفاء) a conjunction; (ينظروا) is like (يسيروا) and is conjoined to it; (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna, the deficient — abrogating (nāsikh) — past verb; (عاقبة) the noun of kāna, nominative; (الّذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (من قبلهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative.. and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), for emphasis; (دار) a mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الآخرة) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (خير) a khabar, nominative; (اللام) a preposition; (الّذين) a relative in the position of the genitive, attached to (خير); (اتّقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and (الواو) the fāʿil; (أفلا) is like (أفلم), the particle [لا] not making the verb jussive; (تعقلون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and (الواو) the fāʿil.
The clause «ما أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause «قل ...».
The clause «نوحي إليهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (رجالا) «[Note: the clause has the status of a single word; that is why it comes before the prepositional phrase (من أهل..) in qualifying.]».
The clause «لم يسيروا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أرسلنا» «[Note: according to the view of al-Zamakhsharī, it is conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "were they given the means, yet did not travel?"]».
The clause «ينظروا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «يسيروا».
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from direct governance by the interrogative (كيف).
The clause «دار الآخرة خير ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الّذين).
The clause «تعقلون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Are you ignorant, so that you do not reason?"

safi-cedvel:75-75.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (جزاؤه) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).. and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "clear" or "evident" or "known".. etc. [Note: Some parsed it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the thing asked about" ... This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, and Abū Ḥayyān rejected it because this implied form carries no great benefit.
2- Or it is a relative noun in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (جزاؤه), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "his recompense is the imprisonment of the one in whose saddlebag it is found", or "the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found" ... and the clause هو جزاؤه is an affirmation of a ruling, so it is resumptive; this is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān.]; (من) a conditional noun making jussive «2», indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (وجد) a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "it", i.e. the measuring cup; (في رحله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وجد), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (هو) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, in the position of nominative — i.e. the imprisonment or the enslavement —; (جزاؤه) khabar, nominative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الكاف) a preposition of comparison [Note: Or a noun meaning "like", in the position of accusative, a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar.]; (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is نجزي ...
and (اللام) is for distance, and (الكاف) for address; (نجزي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "we"; (الظّالمين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «جزاؤه (بيّن) ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «من وجد ...» has no grammatical position: an explanation of what preceded [Note: Or it is the khabar, if (من) is a relative noun, as stated in note no. (2).].
The clause «وجد ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «هو جزاؤه ...» is in the position of jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «نجزي ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.

safi-cedvel:76-76.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunctive; (بدأ) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Joseph — or his agent —; (بأوعيتهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بدأ).. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قبل) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (بدأ); (وعاء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (أخي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (استخرجها) like بدأ.. and (ها) mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من وعاء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استخرجها); (أخيه) like the first; (كذلك) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse (75).]; (كدنا) a past verb.. and (نا) a pronoun, the fāʿil; (ليوسف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كدنا) by making it carry the meaning of "We arranged", the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (ما) negating; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its subject (ism) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he", i.e. Joseph; (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd) and disavowal; (يأخذ) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (أخاه) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (في دين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأخذ); (الملك) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأخذ..) is in the position of genitive governed by the lām, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna.
(إلّا) a particle of exception; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative; (يشاء) an imperfect verb, accusative; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يشاء ...) is in the position of accusative as an exception of the disjoined kind (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) «1».
(نرفع) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "we", for majesty; (درجات) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (نرفع) [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "We raise him a firmly established raising".]; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi; (نشاء) like نرفع; (الواو) conjunctive; (فوق) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (كلّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (ذي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (علم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (عليم) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative.
The clause «بدأ بأوعيتهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"So they were brought back to Joseph, and he began with their bags ..."
The clause «استخرجها ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause بدأ.
The clause «كدنا ليوسف ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما كان ليأخذ ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يأخذ أخاه ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يشاء الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «نرفع ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «فوق كلّ.. عليم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نرفع ...

* Morphology:
(أوعية): plural of وعاء, a noun for that in which a thing is held and kept; its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ. The hamza is changed from a yāʾ; its original form is وعاي, because the plural is أوعية. When the yāʾ came at the end after a quiescent alif, it was changed to hamza, and it became وعاء. The plural of the plural is أواع.
(كدنا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its original form is كيدنا. When the verb was made indeclinable on sukūn because of the attachment of the first-person plural pronoun, the yāʾ was deleted to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters; its pattern is فلنا with kasra on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إن) a conditional particle making jussive; (يسرق) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is "he"; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (سرق) a past verb; (أخ) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma; (اللام) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of أخ; (من) a preposition; (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (سرق); (الفاء) conjunctive; (أسرّها) like سرق ... and (ها) an object pronoun; (يوسف) fāʿil, nominative, prevented from nunation because it is a proper name and foreign; (في نفسه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسرّ)..
and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (يبدها) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter.. and (ها) an object pronoun, and the fāʿil is "he"; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يبدها); (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he"; (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (شرّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (مكانا) tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunctive; (الله) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أعلم) khabar, nominative; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the clause after it being the ṣila (relative clause) and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. تصفونه.]; (تصفون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تصفون) is in the position of genitive governed by the bāʾ, attached to (أعلم).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إن يسرق ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قد سرق أخ ...» is in the position of jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أسرّها يوسف ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لم يبدها ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أسرها.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أنتم شرّ ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported.
The clause «الله أعلم ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.
The clause «تصفون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(أعلم): this adjective is not meant as a true elative (tafḍīl); rather it has the meaning of the active participle, i.e. "knowing".

safi-cedvel:78-78.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (العزيز) badal (substitute) of أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in form; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) —; (اللام) a preposition; (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of inna; (أبا) the subject (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa; (شيخا) naʿt (adjective) of (أبا), accusative; (كبيرا) a second naʿt, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (خذ) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you"; (أحد) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (مكانه) a second mafʿūl bihi, by making خذ carry the meaning of اجعل ("make") [Note: Or an adverb of place attached to (خذ).], and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّا) like the first.. and (نا) a pronoun, the subject of inna; (نراك) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (الكاف) an object pronoun, and the fāʿil is "we"; (من المحسنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يا أيّها العزيز ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical [Note: Or it is the speech reported, and the clause إنّ له أبا is the answer to the vocative, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «إنّ له أبا ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «خذ ...» is in the position of jussive: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if someone must be taken, then take one of us" ...
The clause «إنّا نراك ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «نراك ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.

safi-cedvel:79-79.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he"; (معاذ) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being أعوذ ("I seek refuge"); (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative; (نأخذ) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is "we"; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), by making معاذ الله carry the meaning of "it is not proper and not permissible"..; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وجدنا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (متاعنا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative ...
and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi; (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وجدنا), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse (78).]; (إذا) a particle of response with no governing effect; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (ظالمون) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «(أعوذ) معاذ ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نأخذ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نأخذ) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "from our taking".. attached to (معاذ); and the clause «وجدنا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «إنّا ... لظالمون» has no grammatical position: an explanation of an implied condition together with its apodosis, i.e. "if we took (another) in his place, we would do wrong" ...

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (دخل) past verb; (معه) an adverb (mafʿūl fīhi), accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (دخل).. and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (السجن) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (فتيان) fāʿil (agent), nominative, its sign of the nominative being the alif; (قال) like دخل; (أحدهما) agent, nominative, and (هما) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّي أراني) like إنّا لنراها «1», and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), and the agent is "I"; (أعصر) imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "I"; (خمرا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (قال الآخر ...
أحمل) like the preceding; (فوق) adverb of place, accusative, attached to (أحمل) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (خبزا).]; (رأسي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ, and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (خبزا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (تأكل) imperfect verb, nominative; (الطير) agent, nominative; (من) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تأكل); (نبّئنا) imperative verb.. and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "you"; (بتأويله) preposition and its genitive noun, and muḍāf ilayhi, attached to (نبّئ); (إنّا نراك من المحسنين) like إنّا لنراها في ضلال «3», and its sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «دخل.. فتيان» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an omitted resumptive clause, i.e. "so Yūsuf was imprisoned, and two young men entered the prison with him"..
The clause «قال أحدهما ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّي أراني ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أراني أعصر ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «أعصر خمرا» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl [Note: some permitted the clause to be a second object, because the seeing is of the type of seeing of the heart (ruʾya qalbiyya).].
The clause «قال الآخر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قال أحدهما.
The clause «إنّي أراني ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «أراني أحمل ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «أحمل.. خبزا» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl — or a second object — and the clause «تأكل الطير منه» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (خبزا).
The clause «نبّئنا بتأويله» has no grammatical position, resumptive, within the scope of the saying.
The clause «إنّا تراك ...» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic wording is نراك] has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya) — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — and the clause «نراك من المحسنين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(خبزا): a non-derived (jāmid) noun; its wazn is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The loose metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «إِنِّي أَرانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً», i.e. grapes. The relation is what it will become: grapes were called wine because they become wine, since that is what the pressing is intended for. It is also said that khamr literally means grapes in the dialect of ʿUmān. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: أعصر عنبا.

safi-cedvel:37-38.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) past verb, and the agent is "he", i.e. Yūsuf; (لا) negative particle; (يأتيكما) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (كما) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (طعام) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (ترزقانه) passive imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, and (الألف) a pronoun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi; (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (نبأت) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (التاء) agent, and (كما) a pronoun like the first; (بتأويله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نبّأت)..
and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قبل) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (نبّأت); (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يأتيكما) imperfect verb, accusative.. and (كما) like the first, and the agent is "it", i.e. the food.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتيكما) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).. and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address, and (ما) a particle for the dual; (من) preposition; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to the predicate of the mubtadaʾ, and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. "my Lord taught it to me"; (علّمني) past verb, and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) mafʿūl bihi; (ربّي) agent, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; (تركت) like نبّأت; (ملّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (قوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا) like the first; (يؤمنون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the agent; (بالله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb يؤمنون; (الواو) conjunction; (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (بالآخرة) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كافرون); (هم) like the first and a tawkīd (emphasis) of it; (كافرون) khabar (predicate), nominative, its sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لا يأتيكما طعام ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ترزقانه ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of طعام.
The clause «نبّأتكما» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of طعام [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from طعام, because it is qualified by the clause.].
The clause «يأتيكما» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «ذلكما ممّا علّمني ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption — or causal (taʿlīliyya) — and the clause «علّمني ربّي» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّي تركت ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تركت ملّة ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «لا يؤمنون بالله» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of قوم.
The clause «هم.. كافرون» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause لا يؤمنون.
(الواو) conjunction; (اتّبعت ملّة آبائي) like تركت ملّة قوم, and the sign of the accusative of آباء is the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إبراهيم) badal (substitute) of آباء, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, and likewise (إسحاق، يعقوب), conjoined to it by the two conjunctions; (ما) negative particle; (كان) incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator; (اللام) preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted predicate of kāna; (أن نشرك) like أن يأتي, and the agent is "we"; (باللَّه) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نشرك); (من) redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (شيء) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نشرك..) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of kāna.
(ذلك من فضل..) like ذلكما ممّا علّمني; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (على) preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to فضل; (الواو) conjunction; (على الناس) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what (علينا) is attached to, because it is conjoined to it; (الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for rectification (istidrāk); (أكثر) the noun of lākinna, accusative; (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا يشكرون) like لا يؤمنون.
The clause «اتّبعت ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause تركت.
The clause «ما كان لنا ...» has no grammatical position, causal.
The clause «نشرك ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «ذلك من فضل الله..» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «لكنّ أكثر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ذلك من فضل الله.
The clause «لا يشكرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle; (صاحبي) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb), its sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (السجن) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (أرباب) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (متفرّقون) naʿt (adjective) of أرباب, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the wāw; (خير) khabar (predicate), nominative; (أم) a conjunction equivalent to the interrogative hamza (muʿādila); (الله) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أرباب, nominative; (الواحد) naʿt of the Name of Majesty; (القهّار) a second naʿt, nominative.
The vocative clause «يا صاحبي ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أأرباب.. خير» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.

* Morphology:
(متفرّقون): plural of متفرّق, active participle from the five-letter verb تفرّق; its wazn is متفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(القهّار): one of the intensive forms (ṣiyagh al-mubālagha); its wazn is فعّال, from the three-letter verb قهر.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative; (تعبدون) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من دونه) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أسماء.
and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أسماء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (سمّيتموها) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, the agent, and (الواو) redundant (zāʾida), following the vowel of the mīm, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (أنتم) a detached pronoun, a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun that is the agent of the verb, in the position of nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (آباؤكم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the agent pronoun, nominative.. and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (ما) like the first; (أنزل) past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, agent, nominative; (الباء) preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for worshipping them"; (من سلطان) like من شيء «1»; (إن) negative particle; (الحكم) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (إلّا) like the first; (لله) preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (أمر) past verb, and the agent is "He"; (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (لا) negative; (تعبدوا) imperfect verb, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent; (إلّا) like the first; (إيّاه) a detached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, governed by تعبدوا.
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تعبدوا..) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi governed by أمر, and it is the second object; as for the first, it is omitted, i.e. "He commanded people not to worship a god other than Allah".. or "to worship Allah".
(ذلك) demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, and the reference is to tawḥīd (the affirmation of Divine oneness); (الدين) khabar, nominative; (القيّم) naʿt (adjective) of الدين, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ ... لا يعلمون) like لكنّ ... يشكرون «2».
The clause «ما تعبدون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «سمّيتموها» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of أسماء.
The clause «ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان» is in the position of accusative as a second naʿt of أسماء [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the object pronoun in (سمّيتموها).].
The clause «إن الحكم إلّا لله» has no grammatical position, resumptive, giving the reason for what preceded.
The clause «أمر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive, another reason.
The clause «ذلك الدين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ أكثر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ذلك الدين.
The clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

safi-cedvel:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(حتّى) a particle of inception (ibtidāʾ); (إذا) an adverb of future time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاءهم); (استيئس) a past verb; (الرسل) a fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) a conjunction; (ظنّوا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (أنّهم) a particle resembling the verb ...
and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (كذبوا) a past verb, passive.. and (الواو) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (جاء) is like (استيئس), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نصرنا) a fāʿil, nominative.. and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) a conjunction; (نجّي) a past verb, passive; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; (نشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil being "We" (نحن), for majesty; (الواو) resumptive «[Note: or circumstantial, and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).]»; (لا) negative; (يردّ) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative; (بأسنا) the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative.. and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (عن القوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يردّ); (المجرمين) a naʿt (adjective) of (القوم), genitive (majrūr), its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «استيئس الرسل ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ظنّوا ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause «استيئس الرسل».
The clause «قد كذبوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قد كذبوا..) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of (ظنّوا)..
The clause «جاءهم نصرنا ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to a non-jussive condition.
The clause «نجّي من نشأ ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
The clause «نشاء ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «لا يردّ بأسنا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.]».

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (كان) a deficient — abrogating (nāsikh) — past verb; (في قصصهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان).. and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (عبرة) the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ); (لأولي) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of (عبرة), its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, as it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (الألباب) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (ما) negative; (كان) is like the first one, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), i.e. the Qur'an; (حديثا) a khabar, accusative (manṣūb); (يفتري) an imperfect verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو); (الواو) a conjunction; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative; (تصديق) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (حديثا), accusative; (الّذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; (يديه) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.. and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (تفصيل) conjoined to (تصديق), accusative; (كلّ) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (شيء) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (هدى، رحمة) two nouns conjoined to (تصديق) by the conjunction «[Translator's note: the source has «بحر في العطف», evidently for «بحرفي العطف» "by the two conjunctions".]», both accusative; (لقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (رحمة); (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) the fāʿil (agent).
The clause «قد كان في قصصهم عبرة ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «ما كان حديثا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يفتري ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (حديثا).
The clause «يؤمنون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of (قوم).

* Rhetoric:
1- In the saying of the Exalted «لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ» there is an art to which the ancients give the name mentioned above «[Translator's note: so in the source; no name has been mentioned before this point.]». It is to eloquence what the heart is to a human being, and it is subtle except to those whose natural talents are pure and in whom the faculty of eloquence is abundant. In this phrase there is a variation in the form of the word, by which we mean transferring it from one shape to another, as it is moved from the singular to the dual and the plural. That is in the word «اللب», which is the intellect, not the word اللب that is beneath the husk; for it is not good in usage except in the plural, and so it has come here.
End of Sūrat Yūsuf, peace be upon him.

safi-cedvel:80-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunctive; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلصوا); (استيئسوا) a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (استيئسوا); (خلصوا) like استيئسوا; (نجيّا) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of خلصوا, i.e. "conferring privately together" [Note: In Ḥāshiyat al-Jamal there is the following: «The ḥāl is singular while the one it describes is plural, either because نجيّ is a فعيل with the meaning of مفاعل, like عشير meaning معاشر, and this is always used in the singular — one says "they are your خليط and your عشير", i.e. those who mix with you and those who keep company with you; or because it is an adjective on فعيل like صديق, and it is singular because it is on the pattern of a maṣdar, like صهيل; or because it is a maṣdar meaning "confiding together" ...» End quote.], accusative (manṣūb); (قال) a past verb; (كبيرهم) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ).. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الهمزة) for interrogation; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (تعلموا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (أباكم) the subject (ism) of anna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif.. and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (أخذ) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he"; (على) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أخذ); (موثقا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخذ); (الواو) conjunctive; (من) a preposition; (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (فرّطتم), taking ما as redundant (zāʾida) [Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar-forming particle, in which case the prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), according to al-Zamakhsharī, even though the adverb is cut off from annexation, and the interpreted maṣdar is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū Ḥayyān rejected that decisively, because when the adverb is made indeclinable it cannot validly be a khabar, whether governed by a preposition or not.]; (فرّطتم) a past verb indeclinable on sukūn ... and (تم) a pronoun, the fāʿil; (في يوسف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فرّطتم), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (الفاء) conjunctive; (لن) a particle of negation and accusative; (أبرح) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is "I"; (الأرض) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (يأذن) like أبرح, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى; (اللام) a preposition, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يأذن); (أبي) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأذن) is in the position of genitive governed by (حتّى), attached to (أبرح).
(أو) a conjunction; (يحكم) like يأذن and conjoined to it [Note: Or accusative by an implied أن after أو resting on the negation.]; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (لي) like the first, attached to (يحكم); (الواو) resumptive; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (خير) khabar, nominative; (الحاكمين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «استيئسوا ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «خلصوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قال كبيرهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ألم تعلموا ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قد أخذ ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ أباكم قد أخذ..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of the verb تعلموا.
The clause «فرّطتم ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.
The clause «لن أبرح ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause فرّطتم.
The clause «يأذن ... أبي» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «هو خير ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(ارجعوا) an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلى أبيكم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ارجعوا), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.. and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunctive; (قولوا) like ارجعوا; (يا) a vocative particle; (أبانا) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif.. and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (ابنك) the subject of inna, accusative.. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi; (سرق) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he"; (الواو) conjunctive; (ما) negating; (شهدنا) a past verb indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is the fāʿil; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (شهدنا), the returning pronoun being omitted; (علمنا) like شهدنا; (الواو) conjunctive; (ما) like the first; (كنّا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.. and (نا) a pronoun in the position of nominative, the subject of kāna; (للغيب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حافظين), the khabar of kunnā, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «ارجعوا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «قولوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ارجعوا.
The clause «يا أبانا ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «إنّ ابنك سرق ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported.
The clause «سرق ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «ما شهدنا ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause إنّ ابنك سرق.
The clause «علمنا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «ما كنّا ... حافظين» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause إنّ ابنك سرق.
(الواو) conjunctive; (اسأل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you"; (القرية) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: This is with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "the people of the town"; likewise العير, i.e. "the people of the caravan". If the muḍāf is not implied, the expression is figurative (majāz).]; (التي) a relative noun in the position of accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of القرية; (كنّا) like the first; (في) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the khabar of kunnā; (الواو) conjunctive; (العير الّتي) like القرية التي, and conjoined to it; (أقبلنا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (فيها) like the first, attached to (أقبلنا); (الواو) conjunctive; (إنّا لصادقون) like إنّا لظالمون [Note: In verse (79) of this sūra.].
The clause «اسأل القرية ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.
The clause «كنّا فيها ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (التي).
The clause «أقبلنا فيها ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (التي).
The clause «إنّا لصادقون ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.

* Morphology:
(استيئسوا): the hamza is written on a "tooth" (nabra) because it is vowelled and comes after a quiescent yāʾ.
(نجيّا): a derived adjective on the pattern فعيل, or a maṣdar on the same pattern meaning "confiding together", which is the secret. In the word there is iʿlān [Translator's note: so in the source; iʿlāl (weak-letter change) is evidently meant] by substitution, because the final radical of the word is a wāw, from نجا ينجو, and because the noun is النجوى. Its original form is نجيو — with sukūn on the yāʾ and a vowel on the wāw. When the two came together, the first of them quiescent, the wāw was changed to yāʾ and assimilated into the second yāʾ, and it became (نجيّا).

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنَّا فِيها». Asking the town stands for asking its people, figuratively through the town, since the town is used for them by the relation of the occupant and the place occupied (al-ḥāliyya wa-l-maḥalliyya). The upshot of the meaning is: send someone you trust to the people of the town and ask them about the story.

* Benefits:
1- «وَمِنْ قَبْلُ ما فَرَّطْتُمْ»: in the i'rab of «ما» there are several views that have led the grammarians into a great deal of disagreement, some of it useful and some of it of no real profit. The first: it is redundant (zāʾida) — this is the view of Ibn Hishām — i.e. for the beautification of the wording. The second: it is maṣdar-forming, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ. The third: it is a relative, and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ.
I reckon that if we adopt the first view, it is easier to understand and requires less supposition..

safi-cedvel:83-84.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb; (بل) a particle of digression (iḍrāb) [Note: There is omitted speech before بل so that the digression with it is valid, i.e. "the matter is not really as you have reported; rather your souls have enticed you".]; (سوّلت) a past verb, and (التاء) for the feminine; (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سوّلت); (أنفسكم) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).. and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أمرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الفاء) conjunctive; (صبر) the khabar (predicate) of a necessarily omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being صبري ("my patience"); (جميل) naʿt (adjective) of صبر, nominative like it; (عسى) an inflexible (jāmid), incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (الله) the Divine Name, the subject (ism) of ʿasā, nominative; (أن يأتي) like أن نأخذ in verse (79), and the fāʿil is "He", and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) an object pronoun; (بهم) like لكم, attached to (يأتي); (جميعا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the genitive pronoun in (بهم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتيني ...) is in the position of accusative: the khabar of ʿasā.
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the subject of inna; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (العليم) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الحكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «سوّلت لكم أنفسكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the clause of the speech reported is omitted [Note: There is omitted speech before بل so that the digression with it is valid, i.e. "the matter is not really as you have reported; rather your souls have enticed you".].
The clause «(صبري) صبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause سوّلت ...
The clause «عسى الله ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «يأتيني بهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the verse is أن].
The clause «إنّه هو العليم ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «هو العليم ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.
(الواو) conjunctive; (تولّى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is "he"; (عن) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تولّى); (الواو) conjunctive; (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he"; (يا) a particle of vocative and lament; (أسفى) the one lamented over (munādā mutaḥassar bihi), a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the alif, and (الألف), changed from a yāʾ, is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (على يوسف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أسف [Note: Or attached to (يا), which carries the meaning of "I lament".]; (الواو) resumptive; (ابيضّت) like سوّلت; (عيناه) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif ... and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (من الحزن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ابيضّت), من being causal; (الفاء) conjunctive; (هو كظيم) like هو العليم.
The clause «تولّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال ...
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تولّى.
The vocative clause «النداء ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ابيضّت عيناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو كظيم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ابيضّت عيناه.

* Morphology:
(أسفى): the alif is written short, in the form of a yāʾ, because it is a substitute for the yāʾ. Its original form is يا أسفي, with kasra on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the yāʾ; when prolonging the voice was intended, the fāʾ was given fatḥa, and the yāʾ was changed to alif because it was vowelled and preceded by a fatḥa.
(الحزن): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb حزنه يحزنه, of the نصر class; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(كظيم): an intensive adjective (ṣifat mubālagha) from كظم يكظم, of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعيل. It may validly be a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective), even though the verb is transitive by itself, because grief stayed with Jacob for a long time.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَابْيَضَّتْ عَيْناهُ مِنَ الْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ».
The filling of his heart with grief over Joseph is likened to the filling of a waterskin with water, and he, in his patience and his refraining from complaining to anyone other than Allah, is likened to one who ties up the mouth of a waterskin full of water so that nothing comes out of it; and this is the meaning of al-kaẓm (suppressing).

* Benefits:
- «يا أَسَفى عَلى يُوسُفَ».
This is a kind of expressing pain and distress that falls under the chapter of lamentation (nudba). They permitted three ways for the end of the lamented addressee (al-munādā al-mandūb):
a- That it end with an added alif to emphasise the distress and pain, as in «وا كبدا».
b- That it end with the added alif and the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt), as in «وا حسيناه».
c- That you leave it as it is, as in «وا فلان».
If the lamented one is annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, you may delete the yāʾ and add the alif of lamentation, or you may change the yāʾ to alif, as in «يا أسفا على يوسف», just as you may give the yāʾ fatḥa, as in «وا أسفي».
There is not in this brief note enough to quench the thirst of the thirsty, so let whoever seeks more return to the lengthy works among the books of grammar.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(يا صاحبي السجن) its i'rab has passed [Note: in āya (39) of this sūra.]; (أمّا) particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl); (أحدكما) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative.. and (كما) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) [Note: this fāʾ has been moved back from a forward position; the origin is: مهما يكن من أمر فأحدكما يسقي (whatever the case may be, one of you will pour).]; (يسقي) imperfect verb [Translator's note: the source repeats "imperfect" (مضارع مضارع)], nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the agent is "he"; (ربّه) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (خمرا) second mafʿūl bihi [Note: It is stated in Lisān al-ʿArab: "سقاه الله الغيث وأسقاه (Allah gave him rain to drink).. and one says: سقيته for his lip, and أسقيته for his riding animal and his land.. Sībawayh: سقاه and أسقاه — he made for him water or a watering (suqyā, with kasra on the sīn); so سقاه is like كساه, and أسقى is like ألبس. Abū al-Ḥasan holds that faʿaltu and afʿaltu are equivalent, and that (afʿaltu) is not transferred from faʿaltu by some shade of meaning, as أدخلت is transferred" — end quote. So the verb is transitive to two objects, as you see.], accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (أمّا الآخر) like أما أحدكما; (الفاء) linking; (يصلب) passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he); (الفاء) conjunction; (تأكل) imperfect verb, nominative; (الطير) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (من رأسه) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأكل), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (قضي) passive past verb; (الأمر) deputy agent, nominative; (الذي) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of الأمر; (في) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تستفتيان), which is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn.. and (الألف) the agent.
The vocative clause «يا صاحبي ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أحدكما فيسقي ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يسقي ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أحدكما).
The clause «الآخر فيصلب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «يصلب..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الآخر).
The clause «تأكل الطير ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يصلب.
The clause «قضي الأمر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تستفتيان» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (قال) past verb, and the agent is "he", i.e. Yūsuf; (اللام) preposition; (الذي) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قال); (ظنّ) past verb, and the agent is "he", i.e. Yūsuf; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of anna; (ناج) the predicate of anna, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the tanwīn, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); (من) preposition and (هما) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ناج; (اذكرني) imperative verb, and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the agent is "you"; (عند) adverb, accusative, attached to (اذكر); (ربّك) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive.. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه ناج..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّ.
(الفاء) conjunction; (أنساه) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif.. and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi; (الشيطان) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (ذكر) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ربّه) like ربّك; (الفاء) conjunction; (لبث) like قال; (في السجن) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (لبث); (بضع) adverb of time, accusative, substituting for the explicit adverb, attached to (لبث); (سنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ظنّ ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «اذكرني ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنساه الشيطان» has no grammatical position, conjoined to something implied, i.e. "so he went out, and [Satan] made him forget" [Note: if the third-person pronoun in (أنساه) refers to Yūsuf, then the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.] ...
The clause «لبث ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنساه الشيطان.

* Morphology:
(ناج): active participle from the three-letter verb نجا; its wazn is فاعل. It contains a weakness change by deletion (iʿlāl bil-ḥadhf), for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ) whose weak letter was dropped to suit the tanwīn. Before the deletion the weak letter was a yāʾ converted from a wāw; its origin is الناجو — with kasra on the jīm — the wāw was changed to yāʾ because the letter before it has kasra.. then the yāʾ was dropped for the tanwīn.
(بضع): an indefinite term (kināya) for a number ranging between three and nine; it is masculine with the feminine and vice versa, and is used alone, compounded, and with something conjoined to it; its wazn is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.

* Benefits:
Suspension (al-taʿlīq) and cancellation (al-ilghāʾ) in the verbs of the heart:
In this āya occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted وَقالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ناجٍ مِنْهُمَا. We say: the verb ظن is transitive to two objects; it has been suspended from governing, and its two objects did not appear. But the interpreted maṣdar from anna, its noun and its predicate (أنه ناج) stood in place of the two objects. We will clarify this rule because of its importance and subtlety:
Suspension is the cancelling of the government of the verbs of the heart in wording, not in position, because of the presence of an impediment that prevents them from governing; so the clause is in the position of accusative, standing in place of one object or more. These are the places of suspension:
1- That the verb be followed by something that has the right of first position (ṣadāra), which here is interrogation, the lām of the inceptive (lām al-ibtidāʾ), or the lām of the oath.
For example: علمت أين أخوك (I knew where your brother is), قلت لعليّ أحبّ إليّ [Translator's note: so in the source; the standard example is ظننت لعليّ أحبّ إليّ], ولقد علمت لتأتينّ منيتي (I have surely known that my death will come to me).
2- That it be followed by one of the negative particles, such as: وجدت لا المدّعي صادق ولا المدّعى عليه (I found neither the plaintiff truthful nor the defendant). So the clauses in all the preceding examples stood in place of the objects.
As for cancellation, it is the cancelling of government in wording and position. That is permissible when the verb comes between the two objects or after them. For example: خالدا ظننت مسافرا or خالد ظننت مسافر (Khālid, I thought, is travelling), خالدا مسافرا ظننت or خالد مسافر ظننت. If the verb is in the middle, cancellation and government are equal; but if the verb comes after, cancellation is better.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (قال الملك إنيّ أرى) like قال أحدهما إنّي أراني [Note: in āya (36) of this sūra.]; (سبع) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (بقرات) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (سمان) naʿt (adjective) of بقرات, genitive; (يأكلهنّ) imperfect verb, nominative.. and (هنّ) an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (سبع) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (عجاف) naʿt of سبع, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (سبع سنبلات) like سبع بقرات, for it is conjoined to it; (خضر) naʿt of سنبلات, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (أخر) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to سبع سنبلات, accusative, and it is barred from tanwīn because it is an adjective diverted (maʿdūl) from the form آخر [Note: it was diverted from (آخر), with fatḥa on the khāʾ, which is masculine singular, to the plural (أخر) — i.e. the plural of أخرى — contrary to analogy, because the elative noun, when neither in construct nor bearing (ال), must remain masculine singular.]; (يابسات) naʿt of أخر [Note: it is an adjective standing in for a qualified noun, i.e. سنبلات أخر يابسات (other ears, dry).]; (يا) vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الملأ) badal (substitute) of أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in wording; (أفتوني) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent, and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; (في رؤياي) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أفتوا), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "in the interpretation of my vision"..
its sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إن) jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of kāna; (اللام) redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening (taqwiya); (الرؤيا) genitive in form, accusative in position, a fronted mafʿūl bihi, its sign of the genitive being the implied kasra; (تعبرون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the agent.
The clause «قال الملك ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّي أرى ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أرى ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «يأكلهنّ» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of بقرات [Note: or in the position of accusative as a naʿt of سبع.. It is permissible for the clause to be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from سبع or from بقرات, since they have been qualified; and some take seeing in a dream to be of the heart (qalbiyya), so the clause is a second object.]; and the vocative clause «يأيّها الملأ» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أفتوني ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «كنتم.. تعبرون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are ... then give me your verdict".
The clause «تعبرون» is in the position of accusative as the predicate of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(سمان): plural of سمينة, the feminine of سمين, a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle) from the verb سمن يسمن, of the pattern fariḥa; its wazn is فعيل, and the wazn of سمان is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.
(عجاف): plural of عجفاء, the feminine of أعجف, a ṣifa mushabbaha from عجف يعجف, of the pattern fariḥa and the pattern karuma; its wazn is أفعل, the feminine فعلاء, and the plural فعال with kasra on the fāʾ. عجاف may also be the plural of عجفة, the feminine of عجف, on the wazn فعل with fatḥa on the fāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn, i.e. weak and emaciated.
(خضر): plural of خضراء, the feminine of أخضر, a ṣifa mushabbaha from خضر يخضر, of the pattern fariḥa; its wazn is أفعل, the feminine فعلاء, and the plural فعل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.
(أفتوني): it contains a weakness change by deletion (iʿlāl bil-ḥadhf); its origin is أفتيوني, with ḍamma on the yāʾ before the wāw; then it was made quiescent and the ḍamma was transferred to the tāʾ before it; then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; its wazn is أفعوني.

* Benefits:
- Some grammarians devoted a section to the special features of kāna among all its sisters, and found them to be six things:
a- That it may come as redundant (zāʾida), and its redundancy is under two conditions:
First: that it be in the past-tense form; its redundancy in the imperfect form is anomalous.
Second: that it be between two things that are inseparable.
Most often it is added between «ما» and the verb of wonder, as in: ما «كان» أعدل عمر! (How just ʿUmar was!).
b- That it is omitted together with its noun while its predicate remains. That is frequent after the conditional إن and لو, as in:
سر مسرعا إن راكبا وإن ماشيا (Go quickly, whether riding or walking.)
قد قيل ما قيل إن صدقا وإن كذبا ... فما اعتذارك من قول إذا قيلا
(What was said has been said, whether truth or lie — so what is your excuse for a word once it is said?)
c- It may be omitted alone while its noun and predicate remain, as in the poet's saying:
أبا خراشة أمّا أنت ذا نفر
(O Abū Khurāsha, because you are a man with a band of kin …)
d- It may be omitted together with its noun and predicate all at once, with the redundant «ما» compensating for them all; that is after the conditional إن, as in «افعل هذا إمّا لا..!» (Do this, if nothing else..!).
e- It may be omitted together with its noun and predicate without compensation, as in:
قالت بنات الحي يا سلمى وإن ... كان فقيرا معدما قالت وإن
(The girls of the tribe said: "O Salmā, even if he is poor and destitute?" She said: "Even if.")
And that the nūn of its imperfect may be dropped, on condition that it be jussive with sukūn, and that it not be followed by a quiescent letter nor an attached pronoun, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «لَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا» and the poet's saying:
فإن لم تك المرآة أبدت وسامة ... فقد أبدت المرأة جبهة ضيغم
(If the mirror did not show handsomeness, it has shown the forehead of a lion.)

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا تالله) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (73) of this sūra.]; (تفتأ) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb from which the particle of negation has been deleted, nominative (marfūʿ), and its subject (ism) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you"; (تذكر) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you"; (يوسف) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), prevented from nunation because it is a proper name and foreign; (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (تكون) an incomplete imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتّى, and its subject is a latent pronoun, implied as "you"; (حرضا) khabar (predicate), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون) is in the position of genitive governed by (حتّى), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تذكر).
(أو) conjunctive; (تكون) like the first, and conjoined to it; (من الهالكين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of the second تكون. The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause of the oath together with its answer ... is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «(لا) تفتأ تذكر ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.
The clause «تذكر ...» is in the position of accusative: the khabar of (لا) تفتأ.
The clause «تكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تكون (the second) ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تكون (the first).

* Morphology:
(حرضا): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb حرض يحرض, of the فرح class, meaning "to be on the verge of perishing, and to be ill" ...; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(الهالكين): plural of الهالك, an active participle from the triliteral هلك; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Harmony of wording with meaning (iʾtilāf al-lafẓ maʿa al-maʿnā): in the words of Allah the Exalted «تَاللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّى تَكُونَ حَرَضاً». This device is fundamental in rhetoric; it is the breath of life in the art and the pillar on which it stands. In short, it is that the words of the intended meaning be in harmony with one another, with no word among them that jars or sits uneasily beside its sisters such that it could be replaced.

* Benefits:
- The device of harmonising words with meanings is the summit of eloquence and the peak of the art of clear expression (bayān), and the great and eloquent figures of the community have a wide range in this field, such as the saying of Ziyād: «إن لي فيكم لصرعى، فحذار أن تكونوا من صرعاي» ("I have among you those I have struck down, so beware lest you be among my fallen"), and the saying of al-Ḥajjāj: «إني لأرى رؤوسا قد أينعت وحان قطافها» ("I see heads that have ripened and whose harvest time has come").. And the Noble Qur'an is the speech of Allah; far be it that it should be rivalled in the arena of eloquence or contested in the field of rhetoric. Listen to His words «تَاللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ» — to what extent the harmony between the words of the Book and its meanings has reached.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
