(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he", i.e. Jacob; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (أشكو) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the wāw, and the fāʿil is "I"; (بثّي) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive; (حزني) like بثّي and conjoined to it; (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أشكو); (الواو) conjunctive; (أعلم) like أشكو, but with the vowel overt; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعلم); (ما) a relative noun [Note: Or an indefinite noun described by an adjective ... and the clause after it is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective).], indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi; (لا) a particle of negation; (تعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أشكو ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أعلم ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.
The clause «لا تعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(بثّي): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb بثّ يبثّ, of the ضرب and نصر classes, i.e. "to broadcast and spread" ...; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (بنيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, for it is treated like the sound masculine plural, and the second (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (اذهبوا) an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (الفاء) conjunctive; (تحسّسوا) like اذهبوا; (من يوسف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تحسّسوا) [Note: In the dictionary: تحسّس منه means "he sought news of him".]; (الواو) conjunctive; (أخيه) conjoined to يوسف, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ ...
and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) prohibitive, making jussive; (تيئسوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (من روح) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تيئسوا); (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (إنّه) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الهاء) the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the subject (ism) of inna, in the position of accusative; (لا) negating; (ييئس) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (من روح الله) like the first, the prepositional phrase being attached to (ييئس); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (القوم) fāʿil, nominative; (الكافرون) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The vocative clause «النداء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اذهبوا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «تحسّسوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «لا تيئسوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «إنّه لا ييئس ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا ييئس ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna.

* Morphology:
(تيئسوا، ييئس): the hamza is written on a "tooth" (nabra) because it is preceded by a quiescent yāʾ.
(روح): a maṣdar meaning "rest", which is the heart's relief from its distress; this word was borrowed metaphorically for mercy. Its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Metaphor (istiʿāra): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَلا تَيْأَسُوا مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ», i.e. do not despair of His relief, Glorified is He, and His easing. The original meaning of al-rawḥ — with fatḥa, as al-Rāghib said — is breathing; one says أراح الإنسان when a person breathes. Then it was borrowed for relief, and it is explained as mercy on the basis that it is a metaphor from its known meaning, because mercy is a cause of life, like the spirit (al-rūḥ); and it is annexed to Allah the Exalted because it is from Him, Glorified is He.

safi-cedvel:88-88.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لمّا دخلوا عليه قالوا) like لمّا استيئسوا منه خلصوا [Note: In verse (80) of this sūra.]; (يأيّها العزيز) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (78) of this sūra.]; (مسّنا) a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa..
and (نا) an object pronoun; (الواو) conjunctive; (أهلنا) conjoined to the accusative pronoun, accusative (manṣūb) ... and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الضرّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) conjunctive; (جئنا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (ببضاعة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جئنا); (مزجاة) naʿt (adjective) of بضاعة, genitive (majrūr); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (أوف) an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is "you"; (اللام) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أوف); (الكيل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (تصدّق) like أوف; (علينا) like لنا, attached to (تصدّق); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Divine Name, the subject (ism) of inna, accusative; (يجزي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ ... and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "He"; (المتصدّقين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «دخلوا ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يأيّها العزيز ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «مسّنا ... الضرّ» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «جئنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause مسّنا.
The clause «أوف ...» is in the position of jussive: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you accept it, then give full measure ..."
The clause «تصدّق ...» is in the position of jussive: conjoined to the clause أوف.
The clause «إنّ الله يجزي ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يجزي ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna.

* Morphology:
(مزجاة): feminine of مزجي, a passive participle from the quadriliteral أزجى, meaning "rejected" or "pushed away" because of defect or something else; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn ... The alif is changed from a wāw, because the bare verb is زجا يزجو; when the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, it was changed to alif.
(أوف): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, to suit the indeclinable (imperative) form: the weak letter yāʾ of the imperfect was deleted when it passed into the imperative; its pattern is أفع with fatḥa on the hamza.
(المتصدّقين): plural of المتصدّق, an active participle from the five-letter تصدّق; its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:89-89.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he"; (هل) an interrogative particle; (علمتم) a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and its fāʿil; (ما) a relative noun [Note: It may be a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being the object of علمتم.], indeclinable, in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فعلتم) like علمتم; (بيوسف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فعلتم); (الواو) conjunctive; (أخيه) conjoined to يوسف, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ ... and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (فعلتم); (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (جاهلون) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هل علمتم ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنتم جاهلون ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «فعلتم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما), the returning pronoun being omitted.

safi-cedvel:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (أضغاث) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هي, هذه or تلك; (أحلام) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a negative particle operating like laysa; (نحن) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as the noun of mā; (بتأويل) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عالمين; (الأحلام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الباء) redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (عالمين) genitive in form, accusative in position, the predicate of mā.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «(هي) أضغاث ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما نحن.. بعالمين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the object of the saying.
(الواو) conjunction; (قال) past verb; (الذي) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as agent; (نجا) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is "he", and it is the referring pronoun; (من) preposition and (هما) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of نجا; (الواو) conjunction; (ادّكر) like قال; (بعد) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (ادّكر); (أمّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (أنا) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أنبّئكم) imperfect verb, nominative.. and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the agent is "I", a latent (mustatir) pronoun; (بتأويله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنبّئكم)..
and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause [Note: or linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want the interpretation of the vision, then send me".]; (أرسلون) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent, and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء), dropped for lightening and for the rhyme at the end of the āya, is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «قال الذي ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالوا ...
The clause «نجا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «ادّكر....» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أنا أنبّئكم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «أنبّئكم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنا).
The clause «أرسلون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"Get ready, then send me".

* Morphology:
(أضغاث): plural of ضغث, a noun — originally — for mixed vegetation, like a bundle of grass; then it was borrowed for the false dream. Its wazn is فعل, with kasra then sukūn, and the wazn of أضغاث is أفعال.
(أحلام): plural of حلم, a noun for the dream; its wazn is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn, and the wazn of أحلام is أفعال.
(عالمين): plural of عالم, active participle from the three-letter verb علم; its wazn is فاعل.
(نجا): it contains a weakness change by conversion (iʿlāl bil-qalb); its origin is نجو, its imperfect ينجو; when the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa it was changed to alif.
(ادّكر): it contains two substitutions. The first is the substitution of the tāʾ by dāl: its origin is اذتكر on the wazn افتعل — its bare form ذكر — the tāʾ of iftiʿāl is changed to dāl after the dhāl; then the dhāl was changed to dāl because of the nearness of the two points of articulation; then the two dāls were assimilated and it became ادّكر.
(أمّة): with ḍamma on the hamza, a doubled mīm and a tāʾ with tanwīn; its meaning is a period or a while. A while was called أمّة because it is a group of days, since أمة originally means a group.

* Rhetoric:
1- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ». They put ضغث in the plural, saying أضغاث أحلام, and made it a predicate [Translator's note: the source has «خيرا» ("good"), evidently a misprint for «خبرا» ("predicate"); translated per the evident sense] of the vision, although it was one, for hyperbole in describing the dream as baseless. It is as when you say: "So-and-so rides horses and wears silk turbans", of someone who rides only one horse and has only a single turban.
2- Negating a thing by affirming it (nafy al-shayʾ bi-ījābih): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «قالُوا أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ».
The Creator, Majestic and Exalted, intended to negate specifically [the interpretation of] baseless dreams, as if they said:
"There is no interpretation of baseless dreams for us to know it." And the king's saying to them at first (إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون) serves to indicate that in his knowledge they were not knowledgeable of it, because he used the word «إن», which conveys doubt, hoping they would admit their shortcoming, matching the doubt of the king, who first framed it as a question about whether they knew [the interpretation of] the vision. And the young man's saying أنا أنبئكم بتأويله up to his saying لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون is also evidence of that. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(يوسف) the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun from which the vocative particle has been omitted, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative; (أيّ) badal (substitute) of يوسف, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative [Note: or it is the one addressed by a second, omitted vocative particle.
(2, 3) in āya (43) of this sūra.]; (ها) particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الصدّيق) naʿt (adjective) of أي — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in wording; (أفتنا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter.. and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the agent is "you"; (في سبع) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أفت), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "concerning the vision of seven"..; (بقرات) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (سمان) naʿt of بقرات, genitive — or of سبع —; (يأكلهنّ سبع عجاف) its i'rab has passed «2»; (الواو) conjunction; (سبع سنبلات ... يابسات) its i'rab has passed «3»; (لعلّي) a particle resembling the verb, for hope (tarajjī) — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of laʿalla; (أرجع) imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "I"; (إلى الناس) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أرجع); (لعلّهم) like لعلّي; (يعلمون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
The vocative clause «يوسف ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أفتنا ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يأكلهنّ سبع ...» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of بقرات or of سبع [Note: it is permissible for it to be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the indefinite noun has been qualified.].
The clause «لعلّي أرجع ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أرجع ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of laʿalla.
The clause «لعلّهم يعلمون» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لعلّهم.

* Morphology:
(الصدّيق): see āya (75) of Sūrat al-Māʾida.
(أفتنا): it contains a weakness change by deletion (iʿlāl bil-ḥadhf) to suit indeclinability.. its imperfect is يفتي, with ḍamma on the first yāʾ; its wazn is أفعنا.

safi-cedvel:47-49.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) past verb, and the agent is "he", i.e. Yūsuf; (تزرعون) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (سبع) adverb of time, accusative, substituting for the original adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تزرعون); (سنين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (دأبا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, accusative [Note: or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "persistently", or "possessed of persistence".]; (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حصدتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, the agent; (الفاء) linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (ذروة) [Translator's note: so in the source, for ذروه] imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the agent, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (في سنبلة) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ذروة), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إلّا) particle of exception; (قليلا) accusative as the excepted, from the hāʾ in (ذروة); (من) preposition; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (قليلا); (تأكلون) like تزرعون.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تزرعون ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «حصدتم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause تزرعون.
The clause «ذروة ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined by the fāʾ.
The clause «تأكلون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما), and the referring pronoun is omitted.
(ثمّ) conjunction; (يأتي) imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (من بعد) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي); (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.. and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address; (سبع) the agent of يأتي, nominative; (شداد) naʿt of سبع, nominative; (يأكلن) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (النون) a pronoun in the position of nominative as agent; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (قدّمتم) past verb like حصدتم; (اللام) preposition and (هنّ) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the verb قدّمتم [Note: i.e. what was laid up for people in them; on this view the expression is figurative.]; (إلّا قليلا ممّا تحصنون) like إلّا قليلا ممّا تأكلون.
The clause «يأتي.. سبع» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause تزرعون.
The clause «يأكلن ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of سبع [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from سبع, because it has been qualified.].
The clause «قدّمتم لهنّ» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «تحصنون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
(ثم يأتي.. عام) like ثمّ يأتي ... سبع; (في) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يغاث), which is a passive imperfect verb, nominative; (الناس) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (فيه) like the first, attached to (يعصرون), which is like تزرعون.
The clause «يأتي.. عام» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يأتي سبع.
The clause «يغاث الناس» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of عام.
The clause «يعصرون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يغاث.

* Morphology:
(دأبا): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the three-letter verb دأب; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, and there is another maṣdar with fatḥa then sukūn.
(شداد): plural of شديد, a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle); its wazn is فعيل, and the wazn of شداد is فعال.. There is another plural, أشدّاء, and likewise شدود with ḍamma on the shīn.
(يغاث): it contains a weakness change by conversion (iʿlāl bil-qalb); its origin is يغيث, with ḍamma on the first yāʾ and fatḥa on the second, since the active imperfect is يغيث [Note: the word may also be from الغوث, i.e. يغوث.]. When it became passive and the yāʾ was vowelled, the vowel was heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the ghayn; then the yāʾ was changed to alif because the letter before it has fatḥa, and it became يغاث.

* Benefits:
- The Qur'an is the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
In this āya occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted فَما حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ. In this āya there is a scientific allusion: harvested grain, if it remains in its ear, stays protected from weevils and spoilage — this has been established by experience and science. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, was not a farmer and had no experience such as this, which proves decisively that this Qur'an is not from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, but from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In the Noble Qur'an there are many allusions of this kind, which we will mention in their places, if Allah the Exalted wills.

safi-cedvel:90-90.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الهمزة) for interrogation seeking confirmation (taqrīrī) — or seeking information (istikhbārī) —; (إنّك) a particle resembling the verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the subject (ism) of inna; (اللام) the lām of the inchoative (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (أنت) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: It is better that it be a detached pronoun — not a pronoun of separation (faṣl) — because the word يوسف cannot be confused with an adjective.]; (يوسف) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), prevented from nunation because it is a proper name and foreign; (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he"; (أنا يوسف) like أنت يوسف; (الواو) a conjunction; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (أخي) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (منّ) a past verb; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (على) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (منّ); (إنّه) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse 87 of this sūra.]; (من) a conditional noun making jussive, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (يتّق) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is "he"; (الواو) conjunctive; (يصبر) like يتّق, conjoined to it; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) like the first; (الله) the Divine Name, the subject of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (لا) negating; (يضيع) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "He"; (أجر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (المحسنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إنّك لأنت يوسف ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنت يوسف ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنا يوسف ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported.
The clause «هذا أخي ...» is in the position of accusative: conjoined to the clause أنا يوسف.
The clause «منّ الله علينا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech [Note: It cannot validly be a ḥāl (circumstantial), because of the weakness of the governor, and because the demonstrative refers to one person while the linking pronoun (علينا) refers to two ... It may, however, be the khabar of the demonstrative, with (أخي) a badal (substitute) of it.].
The clause «إنّه من يتّق ...» has no grammatical position: it has the status of a causal explanation (taʿlīl).
The clause «من يتّق ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «يتّق ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis together.].
The clause «يصبر ...» is in the position of nominative: conjoined to the clause يتّق ...
The clause «إنّ الله لا يضيع ...» is in the position of jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا يضيع ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(يتّق): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, to suit the jussive, since the final radical of the word has been deleted from it; its original form is يتّقي, and its pattern is يفتع ... It also contains iʿlāl by substitution, or ibdāl (replacement).. See verse
(21) of sūrat al-Baqara.

safi-cedvel:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا تالله لقد) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (73) of this sūra.]; (آثرك) a past verb, and (الكاف) an object pronoun; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (علينا) like the previous one [Note: In the previous verse (90).], attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آثرك); (الواو) conjunctive; (إن) lightened from the heavy form (inna), and its subject (ism) is an omitted pronoun, which is the first-person pronoun; (كنّا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (نا) a pronoun in the position of nominative, the subject of kāna; (اللام) it is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); (خاطئين) the khabar (predicate) of the incomplete verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تالله لقد ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «آثرك الله ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.
The clause «إن (نا) كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that answers the oath.
The clause «كنّا لخاطئين ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of the lightened (إن).

* Morphology:
(آثر): the madda consists of two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second quiescent, i.e. أأثر, on the measure أفعل, because the imperfect is يؤثر, like أكرم يكرم..

safi-cedvel:92-93.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he"; (لا) of generic negation; (تثريب) the subject (ism) of lā, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative; (عليكم) like علينا «1», attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of lā; (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the khabar of lā [Note: Or attached to (يغفر).]; (يغفر) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative; (لكم) like علينا «3», attached to (يغفر); (الواو) conjunctive; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (أرحم) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الراحمين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا تثريب عليكم ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يغفر الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive within the scope of the speech, as a supplication.
The clause «هو أرحم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يغفر الله.
(اذهبوا) an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (بقميصي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اذهبوا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of اذهبوا.], and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, a badal (substitute) of قميصي — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) —; (الفاء) conjunctive; (ألقوا) like اذهبوا, and (الهاء) an object pronoun; (على وجه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ألقوه); (أبي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ ... and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi; (يأت) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the request, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and its fāʿil is "he"; (بصيرا) a ḥāl, accusative, of the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunctive; (ائتوا) like اذهبوا, and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), (الياء) an object pronoun; (بأهلكم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ائتوا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of ائتوني.], and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أجمعين) a semantic tawkīd (emphasis) of أهل, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «اذهبوا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «القوه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اذهبوا.
The clause «يأت ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ائتوني ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اذهبوا ...

* Morphology:
(تثريب): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb ثرّب; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Metaphor (istiʿāra): in the words of Allah the Exalted «قالَ لا تَثْرِيبَ», i.e. no reproach and no blame «عليكم». Its origin is from al-tharb, which is the thin fat in the abdomen and over the stomach. It was borrowed for blame that tears apart people's honour and takes away the brightness of the face, because when the fat is removed, emaciation and what is displeasing appear, just as through blame faults become visible; so what joins the two is the onset of deficiency after completeness.

* Benefits:
«يَأْتِ بَصِيراً»:
The imperfect verb is made jussive by one of three governors:
a- One of the jussive particles that make a single verb jussive.
b- One of the conditional words that make two verbs jussive: the protasis and its apodosis.
c- A request (ṭalab), whose answer is made jussive.
The signs of the jussive of the imperfect verb are three:
a- Sukūn: if the imperfect verb ends in a sound letter.
b- The dropping of the nūn: if it is one of the five verbs.
c- The dropping of the weak letter from its end: if it ends in a weak letter, as in the verse referred to.
We have passed over giving examples in keeping with the method of the book, so seek these matters in their proper places.

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قال); (فصلت) a past verb, and (التاء) for the feminine; (العير) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (قال) a past verb; (أبو هم) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw..
and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّي) a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) is the subject (ism) of inna; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (أجد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "I"; (ريح) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (يوسف) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (تفنّدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (النون) for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء), deleted for lightness, is a pronoun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تفنّدون..) is in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "were it not that your declaring me senile is existent".. and the apodosis of لولا is omitted, its implied form being "you would believe me".
The clause «فصلت العير ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال أبوهم ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «إنّي لأجد ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أجد ريح ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «تفنيدكم موجود ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تفنّدون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).

* Benefits:
«لَوْلا أَنْ تُفَنِّدُونِ»:
This nūn is for protection (wiqāya); as for the nūn that marks the imperfect verb as nominative, it was dropped after the verb was made accusative by «أن», and the yāʾ of the first person was deleted out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil) and the cadence of the speech.
This feature occurs often in the Noble Qur'an, once by deleting what is present and once by adding what is absent, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: «وَما أَدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ نارٌ حامِيَةٌ», where the hāʾ was added to the pronoun «هي» out of regard for the verse-endings. By my life, the music of the letter and the word in the Noble Qur'an has an effect that surpasses human craft.

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (تالله) the tāʾ of oath and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; (إنّك) like إنّي [Note: The verb ارتدّ can be made to carry the meaning of صار, so that (بصيرا) is a khabar (predicate).] [Translator's note: this note concerns verse 96 (ارتدّ بصيرا), not this verse; it appears to be misplaced in the source.]; (اللام) for emphasis; (في ضلالك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna ... and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (القديم) naʿt (adjective) of ضلال, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تالله», i.e. «(أقسم) بالله ...», is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّك لفي ضلالك ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(القديم): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the verb قدم يقدم, of the كرم class; its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:96-96.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunctive; (لمّا) an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ألقاه), containing the sense of condition; (أن) a redundant (zāʾida) particle; (جاء) a past verb; (البشير) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (ألقاه) a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (الهاء) an object pronoun, and the fāʿil is "he", i.e. the bearer of good news; (على وجهه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ألقاه).. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) conjunctive; (ارتدّ) like جاء, and the fāʿil is "he", i.e. Jacob; (بصيرا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) [Note: In the previous verse (94).] [Translator's note: this note reference appears to be misplaced in the source; the alternative parsing of بصيرا as a khabar of ارتدّ in the sense of صار is printed as a note under verse 95.]; (قال) like جاء; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (أقل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil is "I"; (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أقل); (إنّي) like the previous one [Note: In the previous verse (94).]; (أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (86) of this sūra.].
The clause «جاء البشير ...» is in the position of genitive: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ألقاه ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ارتدّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ألقاه.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لم أقل ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of the first saying.
The clause «إنّي أعلم ...» is in the position of accusative: the speech reported of the second saying.
The clause «أعلم ...» is in the position of nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «لا تعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما), whether nominal or particle.

* Benefits:
- «فَلَمَّا أَنْ جاءَ الْبَشِيرُ»:
The grammarians hold differing views about this «أن», some of them contradictory, and one is at ease adopting the view of those who say it is redundant. Among the grammarians it has several uses:
a- It is accusative-making: it makes the imperfect verb accusative, and it is maṣdar-forming, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar that takes its own position in the i'rab.
b- It comes lightened from «أنّ», and then it occurs after verbs of supposition or certainty.
c- It comes as explicative (mufassira), which is the one that comes after a clause that has the meaning of saying without its letters, as in «فأوحينا إليه أن اصنع الفلك».
d- It may be redundant, conveying the sense of emphasis, as it occurs in this verse. This view was held by Ibn Hishām, al-Ṣalāḥ al-Ṣafadī and many others.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(الر) disconnected letters with no grammatical position [Note: See the first verse of Sūrat al-Baqara (الم).] , (تلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the overt sukūn on the omitted yāʾ because of the meeting of two quiescents, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ, and the demonstrative refers to the verses of the sūra.. and (اللام) is for distance, and (الكاف) for address (آيات) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (المبين) naʿt of الكتاب, genitive.
Clause: «تلك آيات ... » has no grammatical position, inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya).

* Rhetoric:
Mastery of transition (barāʿat al-takhalluṣ): in the noble sūra:
This is a well-known art, widespread in the speech of the eloquent. It is the blending of what the writer or poet presents in elaboration with the first thing with which he began his speech - like the first line of a poem and the first paragraph of an essay - by slipping into it gracefully and with fine meaning, so that the listener does not sense the move from the first meaning until he has already fallen into the second, because of the intensity of the blending and harmony, as if the two had been poured into a single mould; or the writer prepares in it, with one section, for a section he intends to bring after it, or with a subtlety pointing to the meaning of the coming section, as in the saying of the Exalted «نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ». For He, Glorified, prepared with this section for what comes after it of the narration of the story of Yūsuf, peace be upon him, and so made a masterly transition by it to mentioning the story. The subtlety that pointed to describing this story as the utmost in beauty, beyond all the other stories of the prophets mentioned in the Qur'an, is His saying «أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ»: when the addressee hears this description of the story, he is alerted to reflect on it, and finds that every matter in it ended well, every hardship ended in ease, and every severity turned into comfort.

* Benefits:
Reasons for the revelation of the sūra:
1- There are two statements about the reason for its revelation:
a-
It was narrated from Saʿīd ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, he recited it to them for a time, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us a story." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed اللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيثِ. Then they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would narrate to us," so Allah the Exalted revealed الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ up to His saying نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ.
b-
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Jews asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and said: "Tell us about the affair of Yaʿqūb and his children and the matter of Yūsuf." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis - an abrogator - and (نا) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of inna (أنزلنا) a past verb.. and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a nominative, agent, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object (قرآنا) a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), accusative [Note: It is permissible for the ḥāl to come as a rigid word in form because it is a description.. It may also be parsed as a badal from the (الهاء) in (أنزلناه) .] , (عربيّا) naʿt of (قرآنا) , accusative (لعلّكم) a particle resembling the verb, for hope - an abrogator - and (كم) a pronoun, the noun of لعل, in the position of an accusative (تعقلون) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn.. and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative, agent.
Clause: «إنّا أنزلناه ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «أنزلناه ... » is in the position of a nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause: «لعلّكم تعقلون» has no grammatical position, a clarifying resumption, or causal.
And the clause: «تعقلون» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of لعل.

* Benefits:
1- The ḥāl occurring as a rigid word:
It is known that the ḥāl comes as a derived noun, explaining the state of a preceding noun called the ṣāḥib al-ḥāl; the general rule is that the ḥāl comes derived, because of its resemblance to the adjective, and the adjective is something derived. But as we know, every rule has exceptions, and the grammarians have allowed the ḥāl to come rigid if it can be interpreted as a derived word. This occurred in the noble verse in the saying of the Exalted إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا, for قرآنا is a rigid noun and has come as a ḥāl. This is frequent in the language of the Arabs and their modes of expression, and similar to it is our saying (كرّ علي أسدا) , which can be interpreted as (كر علي شجاعا) .
2- Can it be said that there is something in the Qur'an in other than Arabic?
Abū ʿUbayda said: whoever claims that there is a tongue in the Qur'an other than Arabic has spoken what is not true and made a grave claim against Allah. He argued from this verse إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا. It was narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and ʿIkrima that it contains words from a tongue other than Arabic, such as: سجيل - المشكاة - اليمّ - إستبرق. And this is the sound, preferred view. Both views are correct, if Allah the Exalted wills, and the way to combine them is that these words, once the Arabs spoke them and they circulated on their tongues, became eloquent Arabic, even if they are non-Arabic in origin; thus we combine the two views. In the science of the principles of grammar the scholars have established a rule to the effect that if a word or more enters the language of a people, they use it, and it becomes common and used among them, it becomes part of the core of their language, and there is no harm in that; the nations of the earth influence one another and acquire from one another, and this is a universal phenomenon, indeed in all the languages of the world.

safi-cedvel:3-4.t:
* I'rab:
(نحن) a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (نقصّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "we", expressing majesty (على) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (نقصّ) , (أحسن) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the verbal noun because it is annexed to the verbal noun [Note: This is if the word (القصص) is a pure verbal noun, and the object of نقصّ is omitted, i.e. "the story".. But if it is a verbal noun standing in the place of the object - i.e. the thing narrated - then the word (أحسن) is a direct object, and the meaning is "We narrate to you the best of the things narrated".] , (القصص) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الباء) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar particle (أوحينا) like أنزلنا [Note: In the preceding verse (2).] , (إليك) like عليك, attached to (أوحينا) , (ها) a particle of alerting (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of an accusative, direct object [Note: It appears that there is a conflict of operators (tanāzuʿ) in the speech: the verb (نقصّ) and the verb (أوحينا) both seek (هذا القرآن) as a direct object; the second was made to operate and the first was given a pronoun, which was then omitted because it is a complement (faḍla); the implication is: "We narrate it to you ..."] , (القرآن) badal of ذا - or ʿaṭf bayān for it - accusative (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (إن) lightened from the heavy (inna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) (كنت) a defective past verb - an abrogator - and (التاء) is the noun of kāna (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to الغافلين, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa), with no operation (من الغافلين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of كنت, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما أوحينا) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (نقصّ) .
Clause: «نحن نقصّ ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «نقصّ ... » is in the position of a nominative, khabar of نحن.
And the clause: «أوحينا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما) .
And the clause: «إنّه كنت ... » is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl. [Translator's note: the source prints «إنّه كنت»; the Qur'anic wording is «وإن كنت», with the lightened (إن), as parsed above.]
And the clause: «كنت.. من الغافلين» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (إن) .
(إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable in the position of an accusative, attached to الغافلين [Note: It may be attached to the verb قال يا بنيّ in the coming verse.. and according to others than Abū Ḥayyān it is a noun of time, a direct object of an omitted verb, implied "remember ..."] , (قال) a past verb (يوسف) agent, nominative, deprived of tanwīn because of being a proper name and non-Arabic (لأبيه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قال) and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, for it is one of the five nouns, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (يا) a vocative particle (أبت) the one addressed, annexed, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person; the kasra - the kasra of agreement - was moved to the tāʾ which replaces the yāʾ of the first person.. and the omitted (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi (إنّي) like إنّا [Note: In verse (2) of this sūra.] (رأيت) a past verb and its agent (أحد عشر) two numeral parts, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative, direct object (كوكبا) tamyīz (specification), accusative (الواو) a conjunction in both places (الشمس، القمر) two nouns conjoined to أحد عشر, accusative (رأيت) like the first and (هم) a pronoun, direct object (اللام) a preposition and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ساجدين) , which is a ḥāl from the object of رأيت, because the seeing is visual even though it was in sleep.
And the clause: «قال يوسف ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «يا أبت ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «إنّي رأيت ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «رأيت أحد عشر ... » is in the position of a nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause: «رأيتهم» has no grammatical position, a clarifying resumption.

* Morphology:
(يوسف) a non-Arabic, Hebrew name..
(أبت) , the tāʾ that replaces the yāʾ of the first person may be written open (أبت) or closed (أبة), and the tāʾ has a kasra in the reading of Ḥafṣ [Note: It may take a fatḥa on the implication that the yāʾ was changed to alif which was then dropped, the origin being يا أبتا.] .
(أحد عشر) , the word (أحد) occurs only with ten; with the words for the tens (ʿuqūd), (واحد) on the pattern فاعل is used. And see verse (102) of Sūrat al-Baqara for the inflection of (أحد) .

* Rhetoric:
1- In the saying of the Glorified and Exalted «رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي ساجِدِينَ», the mention of the word رأيتهم is not a repetition; it is a resumptive speech on the implication of a question to which it came as the answer, as if Yaʿqūb, peace be upon him, had said to him at his words «إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً»: "How did you see them?", asking about the manner of their seeing; so he said: «رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي ساجِدِينَ».
2- Implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in the saying of the Exalted «رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي ساجِدِينَ», where the things mentioned are likened to rational, prostrating people; the pronoun and the prostration are the indication (qarīna), or one of them is an imaginative indication and the other an embellishment (tarshīḥ).

* Benefits:
- The dream:
This verse contains what proves that the dream is true, and that there is behind it what is behind it. The events of the story came to confirm the dream of Yūsuf, peace and blessings be upon him.
It is reported in the sound ḥadīth from Abū Qatāda, who said: I used to see dreams that made me ill, until I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, say: "The good dream is from Allah and the bad dream is from Satan. So if one of you sees what he likes, let him tell it only to one whom he loves; and if one of you sees what he dislikes, let him spit to his left three times and seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed, and it will not harm him."
There is also what is called aḍghāth aḥlām (confused dreams), which are illusions the sleeper sees as a result of his psychological state, and there is nothing behind them.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, and the agent is "he", i.e. Yaʿqūb (يا) a vocative particle (بنيّ) the one addressed, annexed, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (تقصص) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the agent is "you" (رؤياك) direct object, accusative.. and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (على إخوة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقصص) .. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (يكيدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يكيدوا) in the sense of "they plot" [Note: i.e. "they plot for you a matter with which to scheme against you".. It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq, with the lām in (لك) redundant because كاد is transitive by itself.] , (كيدا) direct object, accusative [Note: or an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq.] , (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative, (الشيطان) the noun of inna, accusative (للإنسان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from (عدو) [Note: or attached to عدوّ.] , which is the khabar of inna, nominative (مبين) naʿt of عدوّ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يكيدوا) is conjoined to an implied maṣdar drawn from the preceding speech, i.e. "Let there be no telling of the dream on your part, and then a scheme from them against you".
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يا بنيّ ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «لا تقصص ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «يكيدوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-like (أن) .
And the clause: «إنّ الشيطان.. عدوّ» has no position, causal. [Translator's note: the source prints «لا محلّ تعليليّة», omitting «لها»; the sense is "has no grammatical position".]
(الواو) a conjunction (الكاف) a preposition of likeness [Note: or a noun meaning "like", in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the verbal noun, being its attribute.] , (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose operator is يجتبيك.. and (اللام) is for distance, and (الكاف) for address (يجتبي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ.. and (الكاف) is the direct object (ربّك) agent, nominative.. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) resumptive [Note: and not for conjunction, because the teaching does not fall within the scope of the likening.] , (يعلّمك) like يجتبيك (من تأويل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعلّم) , (الأحاديث) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (يتمّ) like يجتبي (نعمته) direct object, accusative.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (عليك) like لك, attached to (يتمّ) [Note: or to نعمة, for it is a verbal noun.] , (الواو) a conjunction (على آل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what (عليك) is attached to, so it is conjoined to it (يعقوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote (الكاف) a preposition of likeness (ما) a maṣdar particle (أتمّ) a past verb, and the agent is "he" and (ها) a pronoun, direct object (على أبويك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أتمّها) and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (من) a preposition (قبل) a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of a genitive, attached to (أتمّها) .
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما أتمّها) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose operator is يتمّ.. i.e. "He will complete His favour with a completion like His completing it upon your two fathers".
(إبراهيم) badal of أبويك, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa - or ʿaṭf bayān - (إسحاق) conjoined to إبراهيم with the wāw, genitive (إنّ ربك عليم) like إنّ الشيطان عدوّ.. and (الكاف) in ربّك is muḍāf ilayhi (حكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
And the clause: «يجتبيك ربّك» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative [Note: or it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.] .
And the clause: «يعلّمك ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يتمّ ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعلّمك.
And the clause: «أتمّها ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما) .
And the clause: «إنّ ربّك عليم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive, in the force of a cause.

* Morphology:
(بنيّ) , the diminutive form of ابن. The diminutive returns things to their origins: the alif in ابن is a substitute for a wāw, the origin being بنو, so when the diminutive was wanted the wāw was returned to its origin, being a weak letter, and was changed to yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ of the diminutive, so بنيّ became on the pattern فعيل; and when it was annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, three yāʾs met and one was dropped because of the succession of similar letters, so its form remained (بنيّ) with annexation.
(رؤيا) , a noun for what a person sees in his sleep; its verb is رأى, its pattern is فعلى with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and the alif is written long - although it is fourth - because the letter before it is a yāʾ. Its plural is رؤي on the pattern فعل with fatḥa on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(إخوة) , plural of أخ, a noun with omitted lām, its origin being أخو because its dual is أخوان; its pattern is فع, and the pattern of إخوة is فعلة.
(كيدا) , a verbal noun of كاد, used in the place of a noun; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of certainty (كان) a defective past verb - an abrogator - (في يوسف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the preposed khabar of كان, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa (الواو) a conjunction (إخوته) conjoined to يوسف, genitive.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (آيات) the postposed noun of kāna, nominative (للسائلين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of آيات [Note: or attached to آيات, in the sense of "lessons".] .
Clause: «كان في يوسف.. آيات» has no grammatical position, the answer to an implied oath..
And the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) a noun of time, in the position of an accusative, direct object of an omitted verb, implied "remember" (قالوا) a past verb and its agent (اللام) the lām of inception (يوسف) mubtadaʾ, nominative, deprived of tanwīn because of being a proper name and non-Arabic (الواو) a conjunction (أخوه) conjoined to يوسف, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (أحبّ) khabar, nominative (إلى أبينا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أحبّ) , and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ..
and (نا) is muḍāf ilayhi [Note: In the usage of أحبّ there is some distinction when it is made transitive with (إلى) or with the lām: if you say "Khālid is more beloved to me than Zayd" (أحبّ إليّ), Khālid is more beloved by you than Zayd - i.e. your love for Khālid is greater than for Zayd - and if you say "Khālid is more beloved for me than Zayd" (أحبّ لي), Khālid's love for you is greater than Zayd's love.. In the verse, the father's love for Yūsuf and his brother is greater than his love for their brothers.] , (من) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to.
(أحبّ) , [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here as printed: «متعلّق ب. (أحبّ)», i.e. "attached to (أحبّ)".] (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (نحن) a pronoun, mubtadaʾ (عصبة) khabar, nominative (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative (أبانا) the noun of inna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif.. and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أبانا) the noun of inna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif.. and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: the source repeats the words «أبانا ... مضاف إليه» twice.] (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) (في ضلال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna (مبين) naʿt of ضلال, genitive.
Clause: «قالوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ليوسف ... أحبّ» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «نحن عصبة» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl, the link being the wāw.
And the clause: «إنّ أبانا لفي ضلال..» has no grammatical position, a clarifying resumption.

* Morphology:
(أحبّ) , a noun of preference (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral حبّ, its pattern is أفعل, and the ʿayn of the word has been assimilated into its lām.
(عصبة) , a word indicating more than ten; it was also said: three are a nafar, and if they increase up to nine they are a rahṭ, and if they reach ten or more they are a ʿuṣba; other views were also given. It is of the type of collective noun (ism jamʿ), and the root indicates encompassing, from العصابة (the headband) because it encompasses the head.
